2011.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to describe Chetnik violence as “ethnic cleansing” or use the terms “terror tactics” and “cleansing actions,” with one side citing sources that used the former label and another arguing that sources focused more closely on the Chetniks supported a different section title. They also disagreed about how much context to provide: some wanted to explain Chetnik violence alongside wider wartime violence, while others argued the article should focus on the Chetniks and summarize the violence attributed to them.

2007.summary: Editors disagreed over how to describe Copernicus’s nationality: one argued he should be called a Polish astronomer, while another considered “Prussian” more accurate and noted that readers might associate the term with Germany. Some favored leaving nationality out unless there was broad agreement, arguing that doing so would avoid asserting one side’s position.

2019.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include discussion of a study questioning Calment’s age and identity: some argued the study was unreliable and the discussion should be removed, while others said the controversy was reported in major news sources and should remain. They also disputed whether the controversy belonged in the opening paragraph, with some calling that too much emphasis and others arguing it had become a significant part of the story.

2008.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the article should say that Windows 7’s taskbar resembled Mac OS X’s Dock, with some supporting the comparison and others disputing its accuracy or place in the article. They also debated which screenshots best represented the system: some favored newer images showing more features, while others argued that the article’s main image should use a standard, default setup rather than added software or altered settings.

2007.summary: Editors disputed how to describe Shadow’s age: one account said his body remains 15 while he is chronologically over 50, while another objected to listing 15 without a source. An editor argued that Shadow’s birth year could be calculated from Maria’s stated birthday and age, but another responded that the games’ calendar year was unknown, so the proposed date was unsubstantiated.

2025.summary: Editors disagreed about where to place specialty divisions such as Focus, Searchlight and Sony Pictures Classics in the studios table: one view was that they should not appear alongside the main film units, while another argued they were significant enough to remain grouped with them. The disagreement also concerned whether those divisions deserved their own category or belonged among other brands, with supporters pointing to their industry standing and critics disputing their size and importance relative to major studios.

2011.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include a newspaper’s ranking of The Undertaker’s undefeated streak among sports winning streaks: one objected that it was neither an award nor an accomplishment, while another argued that the cross-sports ranking from a better-known publication merited mention. They also disputed whether a tag-team title win should be described as winning the WCW championship or the WWE World Tag Team Championship, with one editor distinguishing the belts and another arguing that the title’s history continued under a changed name.

2024.summary: Editors disputed how a map should show the Maratha realm’s extent: one argued the existing map wrongly included much of Rajasthan and proposed distinguishing territory held from areas briefly controlled or raided, while another shared concerns about the existing map but said the proposal combined different periods and also had inaccurate boundaries.

2021.summary: A proposal sought to rename the list to include Disney+ animated films, arguing that “theatrical” had originally distinguished them from direct-to-video films, not from a streaming service that did not yet exist. Opponents said the expanded scope would overlap with a separate list of Disney+ original films and preferred keeping this list’s scope while adding an introductory link instead.

2017.summary: Editors disputed whether the opening paragraph should call InfoWars a fake-news site outright or attribute that label to critics, with some arguing it was a derogatory judgment and others saying reliable sources used the description. Some proposed wording that described the site as publishing fake-news stories and promoting conspiracy theories, while another editor objected that a cited source’s “clickbait” classification did not itself establish that the site was fake news.

2013.summary: Editors disagreed over whether material about domestic violence belonged in the article when its sources discussed the issue but did not explicitly connect it to men’s rights activism; some argued the connection was relevant, while others considered it unsupported interpretation. They also disputed how to describe men’s rights activists’ use of feminist language about rights and equality, including whether a critical claim about fathers’ appeals to children’s needs should be stated directly or attributed to its sources.

2021.summary: Editors disagreed over how to translate “Azzurri”: one argued for “light blue” or “Azures,” while others said “Blues” was the established English rendering. Those favoring “Blues” pointed to its use in English-language sources and argued that the team’s nickname should not be translated as a literal name for a particular shade of blue.

2026.summary: Editors differed over whether to list Italy’s expected second match in the qualifying window before its opponent was confirmed: one argued the final or consolation friendly was already scheduled, while another said to wait until the pairing was known.

2010.summary: Editors disagreed over how to present a claim that nearly all historians accept Jesus existed: some wanted the source’s Christian background identified, while others argued the article should follow what the source actually said without implying bias. They also disputed the article’s scope, with some favoring a focus on whether Jesus existed and others arguing it should cover the wider range of views about how much of the Gospel accounts is historical.

2014.summary: Some editors argued that the article should remain a full, separate treatment of evidence about whether Jesus existed, distinct from an article reconstructing his life from historical sources. Others said the subjects substantially overlapped and favored shortening the article to direct readers to related pages, rather than repeating their material.

2023.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the opening paragraph should describe the consensus as belonging to scholarship broadly or specifically to biblical scholars; some also called for softer wording that better conveyed uncertainty, while others said the sources supported the broader description. They also disputed whether a statement that Jesus existed could be read as endorsing divine or supernatural claims: some wanted the article to distinguish a historical human figure from the religious figure, while others argued those questions should be kept separate.

2005.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to place President Bush’s comments about West Bank settlements alongside his remarks on the barrier and future borders: some argued readers should see both, while others said connecting them would imply a link Bush had not made and required a published source making that connection. Opponents of the addition also argued that Bush’s barrier-specific views belonged in the article’s section on international opinions, rather than in its account of the barrier’s history and purpose.

2008.summary: Editors disagreed over whether Sasuke belonged in the list’s “protagonists” section after he was described as wanting to kill everyone in Konoha. One view said his actions made him an antagonist and he should not appear in both lists, while another treated “protagonist” as meaning a main character and favored keeping him with the original Team 7.

2026.summary: An editor proposed changing the article title to Papa Johns, saying the company had changed its name; another replied that earlier move discussions had left the title unchanged.

2006.summary: Editors disputed how the opening paragraph should describe Transnistria: some proposals called it a region within Moldova and emphasized its original declaration as a Soviet republic, while others objected to describing it as a region and argued for its independence. They also disagreed over whether explosions and other violent events should be labeled terrorism; some argued the label was inappropriate without stronger sourcing, while others said it should be included because a Transnistrian security official used it.

2007.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the opening paragraph should call Transnistria a republic or instead describe it as a territory, with some arguing that “republic” was appropriate and others objecting to the label. They also disputed whether it was de facto independent: one view stressed that Moldova did not govern the region, while another argued that its reliance on Russian support undermined that description.

2013.summary: Editors disagreed about whether the Cook Islands and Niue should appear in the lists of states and how their status should be described: some argued they were not fully independent, while others cited sources calling them sovereign and said the evidence did not settle the question. They also questioned whether the pair belonged in a section for United Nations members and observers, since neither was a member or observer.

2005.summary: Editors disputed how to phrase a section about the circumstances surrounding an aide’s death and allegations concerning Scarborough; one proposal called for identifying who made the criticisms and describing an effort to build a case without judging its validity.

Editors disagreed over whether the article should mention claims linking Solana to the Antichrist and the “666” recommendation: one contributor argued for including the topic and said the recommendation was an official document Solana had authored. Others argued that the recommendation was not important enough for the article, and that including it because of its number would not justify its relevance.

2008.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the opening summary’s box should show only Barack Obama and John McCain or also third-party candidates such as Bob Barr, Ralph Nader, and the Green Party nominee; one position favored including candidates who could affect the election, while another argued the extra portraits crowded the box and overstated their importance. Some editors proposed removing all candidate names and pictures until after the election to avoid disputes over who qualified, while others argued that including significant third-party candidates would make the summary more complete and fair.

2024.summary: Editors questioned whether test, ferry and other non-revenue flights belonged on the list, since its stated criteria required paying passengers or cargo carried for hire; one editor supported removing entries that did not qualify. Others argued that the criteria should be changed to include such flights, saying readers look for airliner crashes regardless of whether a flight was for revenue.

2018.summary: Editors disputed how to describe Corbyn’s 2014 Tunisia cemetery visit: some argued the coverage supported saying he laid a wreath at the grave of a Black September figure, while others stressed that Corbyn’s account placed the wreath at a memorial to victims of an Israeli air raid. They also disagreed over whether and how to use the Daily Mail’s reporting, with some calling for its story to be included as the basis of the coverage and others arguing it was unreliable and should not directly support claims in the biography.

2012.summary: Editors disputed whether Henry Ford’s criticism belonged in the article: one argued it addressed Federal Reserve policy and private control, not fractional-reserve banking itself, while another maintained that Ford’s comments about reserve levels directly concerned the reserve system.

2009.summary: Editors disputed how much criticism and controversy belonged in Beck’s biography: some argued that notable incidents and criticism were being left out, while others favored brief, selective coverage rather than a catalogue of critical remarks. They also disagreed over whether to include his earlier negative account of a hospital experience alongside a later statement praising the U.S. health-care system; some saw an inconsistency worth noting, while others considered the comparison misleading or too minor to include.

2010.summary: Editors disagreed over whether criticism of Beck’s Restoring Honor rally could be summarized as accusations of hypocrisy: one objected that the wording generalized from a single critic and did not explain the alleged past behavior, while another argued that several critics implied that charge. A proposed revision instead attributed to African American leaders the view that the rally’s theme distorted the civil rights movement’s legacy.

2006.summary: Editors disagreed over how to describe the reaction to the Wii’s name: some supported noting that it drew criticism, while others opposed including the slang comparison that prompted jokes about it.

2007.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the article should show a worldwide sales total calculated by adding sourced regional figures: some considered it a valid minimum, while others objected that the combined figure was not itself reported by a source. Those opposing the calculation said the figures came from different time periods and that readers seeking a definitive total would be better served by a directly sourced number.

2012.summary: Editors disagreed over how to describe Romney’s departure from Bain Capital, with some arguing that company records listing him as an executive and his board roles suggested continued involvement after 1999. Others said those titles and filings reflected his formal status during a leave of absence, not active management, and argued the article should not imply otherwise without evidence of his role in company decisions.

2016.summary: Editors disagreed over whether and how much to include about a former trainer’s allegation against Manning: some proposed a brief account of the allegation, Manning’s response and a settlement, while another argued that only a single sentence was warranted. They also disagreed about allegations that Manning received human growth hormone, with some opposing coverage as based on weak reporting and others supporting inclusion of both controversies in a brief, sourced form.

2006.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the article should suggest a connection between modern ethnic Macedonians and the ancient Macedonians: one argued that contact and mixing made a link likely, while another said it should not be stated without reliable sources. They also disputed whether the opening paragraph should describe Macedonians as culturally and linguistically close to Bulgarians, with one editor seeking to remove that wording and another defending the relationship and its inclusion.

2007.summary: Editors disputed how many ethnic Macedonians live in Greece, with one side arguing that an unofficial estimate of about 200,000 should be included and another rejecting it in favor of much lower figures and questioning the estimate’s basis. One editor cited a study finding 20,700 Macedonian-language speakers in two regions and argued that the total number of speakers could not exceed 30,000, while noting that not all would identify as non-Greek.

2013.summary: Editors disagreed over whether material about adult entertainment belonged in the article: one defended it as encyclopedic and verifiable, while another argued it did not belong in an article about blond hair and suggested a separate article. They also disputed the Asian hair-color section, with one editor saying its sources did not support the claims and another reporting that the sources supported the section’s basic facts.

Editors disagreed over how the opening paragraph should describe the 2002 Gujarat violence: some wanted to identify Modi personally as a controversial figure because of allegations about his role, while others argued that it should describe criticism of his administration and avoid implying personal responsibility. They also disputed how to present the investigation’s outcome; some emphasized that no formal charges had been brought against Modi, while others argued that this did not erase the continuing controversy over the allegations.

2014.summary: Editors disagreed over how the opening should present Modi’s Gujarat development record: some argued that criticism of uneven benefits was overemphasized alongside economic growth, while others said criticism of unequal human-development outcomes deserved prominent space because it appeared frequently in academic sources. They also disputed whether “human development” was clear wording, with one editor proposing a different description and another defending the term as covering health, education and poverty measures.

2021.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include coverage of Mohan Delkar’s death, with one side arguing the connection to Modi was not established clearly enough and another saying reporting on Delkar’s appeals to Modi made a brief account appropriate. They also disputed whether the article should describe Modi’s administration as broadly considered complicit in the 2002 Gujarat riots or attribute that view to several commentators, and whether academic sources established a consensus on the issue.

2010.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the article should include Japanese titles alongside the English names of game series: one said the alternate names could help readers who use them, while another argued that English-language readers were unlikely to need them.

2014.summary: Editors disputed how much space the article should give to claims linking Nazi-era gun laws with tyranny and genocide, and how those claims should be framed. Some favored a shorter account that attributed the claims to particular gun-rights supporters and noted criticism; others objected that proposed wording could present disputed claims as fact or blur the distinction between a broader argument against tyranny and a more specific claim about Nazi gun laws.

2011.summary: Editors disputed whether the company itself had been renamed Impact Wrestling or only its television program; some called for the company article to return to its former name, while another cited an interview suggesting a company-wide change.

2015.summary: Editors disagreed over how the article should describe scholarly explanations for the South’s shift toward the Republican Party, particularly whether race-driven appeals or suburban and class factors better explain that change. One position held that the race-centered account was the prevailing scholarly view and the suburban explanation a dissenting one; another argued that the suburban account had gained significance and deserved more weight.

2008.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to mention an Ash Ketchum spoof on Robot Chicken: one argued that parody supported including it, while another considered the short clip insufficiently notable.

2012.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to describe Chick-fil-A’s donations and stance as “anti-gay,” as some sources did, or use narrower wording about opposition to same-sex marriage, which others argued was more precise. They also disputed how to characterize an interview in which Cathy spoke of supporting traditional marriage: some editors treated the remarks as opposition to same-sex marriage, while others argued that the interview itself focused on family values and did not mention homosexuality.

2005.summary: Editors differed over whether “Schnorrer” should also be described as someone who seeks handouts, rather than only as a tramp; a reply pointed to a related article defining it as a beggar or sponger and argued that the page should match that description.

2024.summary: Editors disputed whether Yaroslav the Wise’s campaigns in Mazovia belonged on a list of conflicts between Poland and Russia: one argued Mazovia was a Polish state and Yaroslav benefited from the campaigns, while another said they were joint actions with Casimir against Mazovia, not Poland.

2013.summary: Editors disputed applying the label “Megastar” to Mammootty; one editor said sources also used it for Mohanlal and reverted an edit.

2011.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the article should connect Planned Parenthood’s history to eugenics through its founder, Margaret Sanger: some wanted more historical context, while others argued that the proposed material overstated the connection or relied on unsupported inferences. They also disputed how much space to give controversies involving activist sting operations, with some favoring detailed accounts of individual incidents and others arguing for a brief summary.

2009.summary: Editors disputed how to present estimates of the age of the shared paternal lineages among Jewish priests, with one account challenging the published dating method and reporting much younger estimates, while another argued that both published interpretations should be represented. They also disagreed over whether the article’s opening paragraph should foreground the methodological dispute and explain how it changes the estimates, or give more space to the later study’s results.

2008.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the biography should briefly describe Barack Obama’s association with William Ayers and the campaign controversy around it, or leave that material to articles about the campaign and controversy. Supporters argued that continued coverage made the issue worth mentioning in the biography; opponents said it was a partisan campaign attack and did not show a meaningful connection relevant to Obama’s life story.

2009.summary: Editors disagreed over whether Barack Obama’s reported work with William Ayers on nonprofit boards and the criticism it drew during the 2008 campaign merited a mention in Obama’s biography. Some argued that the association’s campaign-related coverage belonged in campaign articles, not the main biography, because they considered it too minor to merit space there.

2010.summary: Editors disagreed over how specifically to describe Obama’s religion in the article’s information box, debating whether “Christian” was sufficient or whether a denomination should be named. Some argued that “Christian” was the best-supported description without a clear statement of his current denomination, while others favored “Protestant” and noted his former membership in the United Church of Christ.

2012.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the biography’s treatment of criticism of Obama was too muted: one argued it should state criticisms more directly, while others said concerns should be raised through specific proposals rather than by comparing the volume of criticism with other presidents’ biographies. They also disputed an unemployment chart: critics said it gave undue emphasis to job gains and losses and used a misleading scale, while another editor defended it as a straightforward presentation of the unemployment rate during Obama’s presidency.

2015.summary: Editors disputed whether the article’s account of Fiorina’s Hewlett-Packard tenure repeated too much negative commentary and should be shortened or balanced with favorable views. Others argued that the account should reflect the greater prominence of critical assessments in published sources, rather than give positive and negative views equal space.

2011.summary: Editors disagreed over how to describe the Cameron Todd Willingham case, including whether Perry had received pre-execution doubts about the conviction and how to distinguish an expert’s disputed opinion from established facts. They also debated whether to mention Perry’s 2007 Bilderberg meeting: some favored a brief factual reference, while others argued its limited coverage did not make it significant enough for his biography.

2023.summary: Editors disagreed over whether Spain belongs on the list: one argued that sources describe it as a regional power in Southern Europe, while another said the cited sources call it a middle power, not a regional power.

2015.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include the transfer of power from Goodluck Jonathan to Buhari: one argued it was not an issue and should be left out, while another said it marked the first democratic transfer of power to an opposition party in Nigeria.

2024.summary: Editors disagreed over whether maps should leave autonomous tribal areas as gaps or shade them to show varying degrees of Mauryan influence: some argued that the sources did not establish complete independence, while others said they did not show these areas as part of the empire. They also disputed the empire’s western extent, with some arguing that maps should include territories said to have been ceded by the Seleucids, while others cited interpretations limiting the ceded area of Gedrosia to its eastern part.

2006.summary: Editors disputed whether the article should be titled “Islamic terrorism” or retain “Islamist terrorism,” with proponents of the first citing its greater use and opponents arguing that the existing title was more accurate. The disagreement turned on whether the wording described violence associated with Islam broadly or actions linked to Islamist beliefs, with one editor warning that “Islamic terrorism” could imply that terrorism sprang directly from the religion itself.

2011.summary: Editors disagreed over whether Anders Breivik’s attacks belonged in an article about Christian terrorism: some cited commentators who applied that label, while others argued his actions were driven by political views or mental illness rather than Christianity. A related dispute concerned whether a psychiatric assessment of Breivik undermined the religious-motivation claim; some editors said it did not resolve that question, while others argued that it weakened the case for including him.

2006.summary: Editors disagreed over whether Naruto’s name should follow English order, with the given name first, or Japanese order, with the family name first. Supporters of English order argued it would be more familiar to English-speaking readers, while supporters of Japanese order pointed to the naming order used in the original Japanese version.

Editors disagreed over whether the article should use “Catholic Church” or “Roman Catholic Church”: some argued the shorter name matched common usage and the institution’s self-description, while others said it could blur distinctions among churches and favored the more specific label. In a separate discussion, editors disagreed over whether popes’ succession from Peter should be stated as historical fact or attributed to Catholic belief, given questions about the early historical evidence.

2008.summary: Editors disputed how to describe the Inquisitions: one proposed text said torture was authorized and listed possible punishments, while another editor argued that these statements blurred differences between inquisitions and could overstate how often people were executed. Editors also disagreed over the opening paragraph’s naming of the Church, with one proposal calling “Catholic Church” its official name and another simply presenting “Roman Catholic Church” and “Catholic Church” as alternative names.

2009.summary: Editors disputed whether historical scholarship supports the Catholic Church’s traditional account of its origins, which connects Jesus and Peter with the early church in Rome, or whether the account’s central claims go beyond what the historical evidence establishes. Some editors cited historians who treated Peter’s Roman role and the church’s continuity as supported, while others pointed to scholarship saying few historians now hold that Jesus founded the church in essentially its present form and questioned whether cited sources supported the article’s broader claims.

2010.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the article should prioritize explaining the Church’s present-day structure and beliefs or give a brief overview that includes its history. Some objected that major cuts removed important coverage of beliefs and practices, while others argued that the article should be shorter and direct readers to separate articles for details.

2012.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the article should be titled “Catholic Church” or “Roman Catholic Church”: one proposal called the shorter title too broad and misleading, while an opposing editor argued against changing it and identified “Catholic Church” as the Church’s official title. They also disputed how to describe the Church’s historical teaching on contraception, with one editor proposing a claim that it had always condemned artificial birth control and others questioning whether the cited material adequately supported that history.

2026.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the article title should include “Crown Prince of Iran”: some argued that the title was no longer in use and that the article should use Reza Pahlavi’s name alone, while others favored retaining the title as part of a naming convention for former royal heirs. They also disputed how to describe his former position in the infobox, with one editor proposing “former” or dates of service to clarify that the title was no longer held, while others argued that the infobox should retain the royal title without that qualification.

2016.summary: Editors disputed whether Ronaldo should receive the 2016 UEFA Super Cup among his listed honours: some argued he was ineligible because he was neither in the match squad nor involved in the game, while others said his membership of the winning club entitled him to the honour. The debate also raised questions about consistent treatment, with a contributor comparing Ronaldo’s case to other players’ honours, including Messi’s 2006 Champions League title.

2017.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the article’s opening paragraph should say Ronaldo was regarded by many, by some, or not at all as the greatest footballer of all time; one proposal was to describe him instead as one of the greatest. They also disputed whether the sources supported that broad characterization or only recorded a few people’s opinions, with some arguing the wording should be narrower and others favoring consistency with similar wording on Messi’s page.

2018.summary: Editors disputed how strongly the opening paragraph should describe Ronaldo’s standing: some argued that reliable sources supported saying he was regarded by many as the greatest ever, while others said the evidence supported weaker wording and warned against treating rankings or selected opinions as broad agreement. Some participants also wanted Ronaldo and Lionel Messi to have matching opening wording, while others argued that the available sources did not justify identical descriptions or the same claim about their standing.

2021.summary: Editors disagreed over when to identify Ronaldo as a Manchester United player: some sought to update the article after news of an agreement, while others argued that the transfer was not final until contractual steps were complete and questioned whether particular reports were sufficient. A proposed update to the legal section was challenged because its wording could suggest a trial over the rape allegation, while its proposer argued that leaving out later legal developments made the account seem settled.

2016.summary: Editors disagreed over whether WWE’s use of “WWE World Championship” on its website and a show marquee meant the title had been renamed, or whether shifting labels were just shortened forms of a longer name rather than evidence of an official change.

2023.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the opening paragraph had become too long and crowded with statistics and descriptions of the city’s importance, or whether it should retain a broad account of New York’s influence across many fields. They also disputed whether to describe the city as a center of glamour: supporters said the wording was supported by published coverage, while critics questioned the term’s meaning and whether the cited material justified including it.

2006.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to describe al-Khwarizmi as Persian or Arab: one cited expert opinion for Persian ancestry despite his Arabic writings and work in Baghdad, while another argued that his Arabic name, writings and life in Baghdad supported calling him Arab. Others proposed leaving ethnicity out of the opening paragraph or presenting both positions, reflecting disagreement over how uncertain origins should be represented in the article.

2005.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the brothers’ discussion of complex numbers and information reflected valid connections in physics or showed a misunderstanding; one participant read the text charitably, while a critic described it as ambiguous and pointed to other passages as evidence of poor scientific understanding.

2007.summary: A discussion challenged the article’s claim that Melina was dating Bautista, while a reply defended including it on the grounds that it was reported in Bautista’s book and was sourced.

2013.summary: Editors disagreed over whether entries could be chosen through editorial judgment or needed reliable published sources that described a death as unusual or otherwise exceptional. An account of the discussion’s formal review said the stronger position was to require reliable sources for that characterization, while some editors argued for editorial discretion instead.

2014.summary: Editors disagreed over how much information about group-stage matches belonged in the main article, including goalscorers, attendance and referees. Some favored limiting it to dates, times, results and venues, while others wanted the extra details kept together during the live group stage and reduced afterward.

2008.summary: Editors disagreed over how to explain the group-stage ranking rules, especially whether to add prose clarifying that head-to-head results could outrank overall goal difference; some argued this would help readers, while others said the listed criteria were already clear and the explanation was unnecessary. They also discussed whether a later tie-break calculation for Romania should be described as a loss by a certain margin or with specific score conditions.

Editors disagreed over whether the biography should explicitly cover criticism of Rawat: some argued that leaving it out made the account unbalanced and that significant criticism should be mentioned, while others rejected blogs, tabloids and other sources they considered unreliable and called for scholarly sourcing. They also disputed whether criticism belonged under a separate heading or should be woven into the account of his life, and how much space it deserved.

2020.summary: Editors disagreed over whether ATK Mohun Bagan FC should have a separate article, with one proposal arguing it was not clearly a continuation of either predecessor club. Another editor argued it legally continued Mohun Bagan FC after the investment and merger, so a separate article was unnecessary.

2005.summary: Editors disputed whether the opening paragraph should say Schiavo was in a persistent vegetative state or more narrowly report that doctors diagnosed her that way, with others arguing that court rulings supported stating the diagnosis as fact. They also disagreed over whether the opening paragraph should mention the competing minimally conscious state diagnosis and doctors’ differing assessments, or leave that detail to the article’s later discussion.

Editors disagreed over wording that presented human common descent as a major debate: one objected that this implied scientific disagreement where, in their view, there was none. Another argued that changes to the section imposed a materialist perspective and that the article should balance religious and scientific views.

2016.summary: Editors disagreed over who held the championship after the July 18 episode of Raw: one noted that Seth Rollins was announced as champion on the show, while the network said the match was a draw and Dean Ambrose remained champion. Another editor argued that WWE’s recap settled the question in Ambrose’s favor.

2017.summary: Editors disagreed over whether title reign lengths should be based on when a title change happened or when it aired, and whether WWE’s official dates should be primary or noted alongside the actual dates. They also disputed whether to list Antonio Inoki’s brief title reign as unrecognized: one editor argued it counted despite WWE no longer recognizing it, while another compared it to overturned title decisions that were not listed as reigns.

2021.summary: Editors disputed whether a cited book supported the article’s account of how Azerbaijanis originated; one editor said it did not and proposed removing the claim pending verification. They also disagreed about including Azerbaijani historians’ views: one called for their inclusion, while another argued that such historians were unreliable and favored Western, Russian, and primary sources.

2007.summary: Editors disagreed over how much of the story to include in the plot summary: one editor proposed adding events involving Mary Jane and Gwen, while another argued that such details were minor and that the summary should stay brief. They also disputed whether the plot summary should call Eddie Brock’s character “Venom”: one editor pointed to the film credits, while another argued that the summary should use names as they are used within the film.

2008.summary: Editors disputed whether Sasuke had the Mangekyo ability: one argued that his bleeding eye and its appearance showed he did not have the more powerful form, while another said the stated abilities did not rule it out; they also disagreed over whether he still possessed Mangekyo after Itachi implanted Amaterasu in him.

2007.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the article should frame electronic voice phenomenon chiefly as an alleged paranormal phenomenon or describe it more neutrally as sounds that people interpret in different ways. Some argued that paranormal interpretations should come first because they explain why the subject is notable, while others said natural explanations stand on their own and should not be presented merely as replies to paranormal claims.

2021.summary: One editor argued that the article should list comparable aircraft, suggesting several jets as possible comparisons. Another said the list had been removed after repeated arguments over which countries’ aircraft should be included.

2020.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include an interpretation linking the name Boro to a saying meaning “great people”: one editor argued it was supported by a cited source, while another said the citation did not establish the name’s origin and that the etymology section should not include it.

2008.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the article should retain a separate section of selected “notable matches,” with one critic arguing the selection was subjective and another defending its inclusion. They also disputed how to present Sharapova’s tournament history: critics objected to extensive match-by-match scores and repetitive prose, while another editor defended the writing style and suggested adding commentary or changing the wording.

2015.summary: Editors disputed whether Jenner should be described with feminine pronouns for events before she came out: some argued her latest expressed gender identity should apply throughout her life, while others favored wording that reflected earlier usage or avoided pronouns. The disagreement also shaped accounts of Jenner’s Olympic history, where editors debated whether specifying that she competed in the men’s decathlon provided needed context or risked suggesting that she was a man.

2007.summary: Editors disagreed over how much of the story to recount: some argued the summary should focus on a few major plot strands and remove minor events, while others wanted a fuller account that preserved details readers might otherwise miss. The disagreement was about whether completeness or brevity better served the article, not about the book’s events themselves.

2019.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include coverage of Carlson’s past remarks about women and, if included, whether to give it a separate section or use a heading calling the remarks misogynistic; supporters cited extensive coverage, while critics questioned the timing, context, and wording. They also disputed whether criticism of Carlson’s racial rhetoric belonged in the opening paragraph: some called it central to his public image, while others said it would give recent criticism too much prominence.

2020.summary: Editors disagreed over whether Carlson’s comments about Kyle Rittenhouse during the Kenosha protests merited inclusion, with some arguing the extensive coverage made them significant and others calling them too recent or one example in a long stream of provocative remarks. They also disputed how to characterize Carlson’s words: supporters of inclusion described him as defending or supporting Rittenhouse, while opponents argued he had only posed a rhetorical question about Rittenhouse’s view and that stronger wording misrepresented the quote.

2006.summary: Editors disagreed over whether earlier Serb losses around Srebrenica should be presented as context for the 1995 massacre: one argued that revenge for those losses may have motivated Serb forces, while another disputed that explanation as an attempt to excuse the killings. They also disputed how to describe Serb casualties, with one editor objecting that the article did not make clear that most were soldiers killed in fighting, and another arguing that the available estimates varied and that the breakdown was uncertain.

2009.summary: Editors disputed whether the article should say Khatris were related to Aroras or instead to groups such as Jats and Tarkhans; one editor urged removing the claimed Arora connection and adding the other relationships, while a reply objected that the claims lacked citations. They also disagreed over how to describe Khatris’ social identity: one comment distinguished Khatris from Kshatriyas, while another argued that Khatris had Kshatriya heritage and had taken up merchant work.

2012.summary: Editors disagreed over how to title and group sections about Chopra’s career, with suggestions including “success and setbacks” and “ups and downs”; one editor argued that film performance did not alone establish her personal success and warned against exaggerating it. Another editor said the revised titles made the article seem too flattering and favored the more neutral “ups and downs.”

2013.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the opening paragraph’s description of Chopra’s versatility and unconventional roles was justified or overly praising, with one side citing media coverage in support. They also disputed how to describe her planned role in *Humraaz*: the producers said she took on other commitments, while Chopra said her pageant schedule prevented her from accepting the role.

2005.summary: Editors disagreed over how much space the article should give to reports questioning IIPM’s advertising claims: some wanted a brief summary or a separate article, while others argued that the controversy deserved substantial coverage on the institute’s page. Supporters of reducing the coverage called the allegations unproven and objected to reliance on blogs, while others said magazine reporting and related evidence justified including the criticism and its details.

2018.summary: Editors disputed whether Karna successfully strung the bow at Draupadi’s marriage contest or failed, with one account also rejecting the claim that he was defeated by Arjuna there. A participant challenged the article’s use of an online translation as a primary source and called for support from secondary sources.

2007.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to report a pharmacist’s recommendation that Quackwatch adopt formal peer review, with some arguing the advice belonged in the article and others objecting that quoting it alone misrepresented the review’s overall tone. The disagreement also concerned how to describe the review: opponents of the proposed wording said it was generally positive and that the recommendation needed fuller context rather than being presented as a standalone criticism.

2015.summary: Editors discussed whether the article should include a list of every league goalscorer: one editor called it an excessive collection of statistics and suggested a separate player list as a better location, while the passage notes that another editor kept restoring it.

2021.summary: Editors disputed whether to describe Musk as an engineer in the article’s opening paragraph: some argued that reliable sources rarely used the label, while others cited coverage calling him an engineer or referring to his SpaceX title of chief engineer. The discussion distinguished a general description of Musk as an engineer from reporting a specific job title attributed to SpaceX.

2025.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include Musk’s inauguration gesture and how to describe it: some argued that it should be reported as an incident widely compared to a Nazi salute, without asserting what he intended, while others disputed that interpretation and cited the Anti-Defamation League’s view that it was not a Nazi salute. They also contested describing Musk as a supporter of international far-right parties, activists and causes; supporters pointed to news coverage, while opponents objected that “far-right” was a loaded or overly broad label.

2010.summary: Editors disputed how much detail belonged in the opening paragraph: some proposed removing lists of boxing websites and past titles, while another comment said efforts to condense the rankings had been reverted in favor of a fuller version.

2008.summary: Editors disagreed over how much space the article should give to voter-registration investigations and employee convictions: some favored a short account, while others argued for substantial detail about individual cases and the number of convictions. They also differed over whether reported cases showed a broader problem within ACORN or wrongdoing by individual employees, with one position cautioning that the organization’s role remained uncertain and the other emphasizing the number and spread of convictions.

2009.summary: Editors disagreed over whether coverage of the undercover videos justified describing the events as a broader controversy: one wanted to wait for independent reporting to support that framing, while another argued that coverage by several outlets and ACORN’s response made it controversial. They also disputed how prominently the episode should appear, with one editor warning against giving the video undue weight and another saying the section was appropriate.

2014.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include Stockman’s policy positions, including on energy and jobs: some argued the material relied on his own statements and lacked independent coverage, while another editor said his positions should be included. They also disputed whether to mention a reported felony charge that was later dropped, with one editor questioning its relevance and another pointing to news coverage and its role in the 2014 campaign.

2016.summary: Editors disputed how to describe Galkayo’s political division: one contributor said the article should state that its northern part was governed by Puntland and its southern part by Galmudug, and objected that another editor’s replacement wording was unsupported by its cited source.

2013.summary: Editors disagreed over whether John Hurt should appear in the article’s main image and actor list: supporters argued that he portrayed a legitimate incarnation of the Doctor, while opponents said the infobox should highlight actors who led the series and that Hurt could be mentioned among other actors.

2018.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to keep the airlines-and-destinations table, with some seeking to replace it with sourced prose and others arguing that the table should remain alongside historical summaries. They also disputed whether announced future routes belonged in the table: some viewed them as temporary travel information, while others supported including them when properly sourced.

2019.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to list future routes: supporters said properly sourced routes should be included, while an opponent argued that some citations should be removed and seasonal charter schedules might not count as scheduled routes.

2008.summary: Editors disagreed over when unreleased episodes should be added to the season list: one argued that future titles should stay in a separate section until a press release confirmed them, while another said “Love Blactually” belonged on the list because it had a press release, though other unconfirmed episodes should remain separate.

2009.summary: Editors disputed whether episode titles from a blog could be added to the list: one argued its past accuracy and claimed connection to the show made it trustworthy, while others said its authorship and reliability were unverified and objected to using it without a reliable source. The argument also touched on a fan wiki proposed for the external links section, with one editor supporting it as a detailed, improving resource and others criticizing its quality and sourcing.

2016.summary: Editors disputed whether the opening sentence should describe Murray as Scottish or British: one side argued that British should come first because he represents Great Britain and identifies as both, while others defended the Scottish wording alongside references to his British identity elsewhere. Supporters of the existing wording said it balanced the two identities, while critics argued that British should be prioritized and Scottish mentioned later in the opening section.

2008.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the opening paragraph should give greater prominence to the view that the Holodomor was genocide: one argued that this view was not being fairly represented, while another said it was covered in the article and that the paragraph should reflect the lack of scholarly agreement. They also disagreed over how much weight to give government recognition of genocide, with one editor citing countries’ declarations as support and another arguing that political positions did not settle the scholarly debate.

2017.summary: An automated edit added archived versions of two external links on the article.

2008.summary: Editors disputed whether the article should list screamo among the genres applied to The Used: one position argued it belonged in a list of classifications despite the band’s stated reluctance to be labeled that way, while another proposed leaving it out because sources conflicted. They also debated how to describe the band’s comments, distinguishing not wanting the label from declaring that the band was not screamo.

2006.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the article’s title should call the claims “conspiracy theories” or use a less loaded description, with one side arguing the label was biased and another defending it as accurate for claims about a conspiracy. They also disputed whether the engineering community could be described as rejecting controlled-demolition explanations: some editors cited publications describing broad professional agreement, while others argued that this wording overstated what the sources established and pointed to engineers who disagreed.

2008.summary: Editors proposing a new title argued that “conspiracy theories” was derogatory and ambiguous, and that “alternative theories” would better cover the article’s range of accounts. Opponents said the existing phrase was widely used for these accounts and was not pejorative in the article’s title.

2005.summary: Editors disputed whether the opening should say that the Gospels present Jesus as God: some argued that the passages are ambiguous and open to different readings, while others said that parts of John state his divinity directly. They also disagreed over whether the article should mainly recount the Gospel narratives and direct readers to other pages, or give more space to historical scholarship and competing accounts of how the Gospels developed.

2006.summary: Editors disputed how the opening paragraph should describe scholars who question whether Jesus existed, including whether it should state that they cite the absence of documents written during his lifetime. Some wanted that reason stated plainly, while others argued that the opening should simply mention the minority view and leave its reasoning to a linked article.

2007.summary: Editors disputed how to describe Jesus’ siblings: one argued that the Gospel passages clearly identify four brothers and unnamed sisters and that the brothers’ names should be included, while another said the wording allows different interpretations and the article should report what sources say rather than decide its meaning.

2010.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the article should distinguish the historically reconstructed Jesus from claims that he was divine or the Messiah, or instead present these as different views of the same figure in one article. They also disputed whether sources supporting the scholarly view that Jesus existed should be identified or discounted because some authors were Christian, with other editors arguing that the scholars’ religious beliefs did not invalidate their historical work.

2015.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the article gave too much space and prominence to the Gospel accounts; one side argued that the historical discussion should come first or be combined with them, following how other reference works present Jesus. Others argued that the Gospels are important sources whose portrayals are studied regardless of their historical accuracy, and should remain in a separate section, presented before historical reconstructions.

2016.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the opening should say that the Gospels are not fully historically reliable: some argued that this was a common scholarly assessment, while others called the wording ambiguous and disputed whether it was supported as a broad scholarly view. Some favored an earlier version that instead emphasized disagreement about the Gospels’ reliability and how closely the biblical Jesus reflects the historical Jesus.

2006.summary: Editors disputed whether Mark Twain’s travel descriptions belonged in the article’s account of population: some argued that his impressions were not demographic research and should give way to academic estimates. Others defended the descriptions as notable firsthand observations, arguing that population figures for the period were uncertain and that readers should be able to compare different sources.

2010.summary: Editors disputed whether the account should be labeled a creation myth, with some arguing that the term is a scholarly category and others preferring a more neutral title such as “narrative” because “myth” can suggest falsehood to readers. They also disagreed over whether Genesis describes creation from nothing or creation from pre-existing chaos, and whether both interpretations should be included.

2012.summary: Editors disputed whether the opening paragraph should call Genesis’s account a creation myth or use wording such as “narrative” or “story”: supporters of “myth” cited its academic use, while opponents worried readers would take it to mean the account was fictional. They also disagreed over how to present literal readings alongside scholarly interpretations, with some editors arguing that the account’s symbolic description need not rule out a literal reading.

2023.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the article should describe EMDR as pseudoscientific without qualification: some argued that this characterization was supported by expert sources, while others said it overstated the sources and overlooked evidence that EMDR is used as an effective PTSD treatment. They also disputed how to present that evidence, with one side emphasizing clinical recommendations and reported effectiveness and the other stressing that sources disagree and that EMDR’s distinctive eye movements may not add benefit beyond exposure-based therapy.

2005.summary: Editors disagreed over whether every named storm should have its own article: one proposal would give each storm a separate page and leave the season article with brief summaries, while opponents argued that many storms lacked enough material and separate pages could remain underdeveloped.

2008.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to keep a section about alleged mistakes in the film: one objected that it copied a single person’s commentary and said some claims misread the scenes, while another defended including the errors and argued they reinforced misconceptions about Hispanic people. Others questioned calling the details mistakes, noting that the film was fictional and the creators may have chosen them deliberately.

2013.summary: Editors disagreed over how to describe violence and the movement’s role in it: one side argued that sourced reports of violent incidents and militant factions should be included alongside accounts portraying the movement as peaceful, while another objected that this gave limited cases too much weight and risked portraying the wider community as radical. They also disputed claims that Barelvi groups were involved in jihad or conflict with Hindus, with objectors calling those claims unsupported and others pointing to sources they said documented particular groups’ activity.

2005.summary: One proposal would group artists into broad sales ranges instead of ranking them precisely, arguing that exact figures and source material could not support reliable ordering. A response favored keeping exact ranks because it saw them as the purpose of a list of best-selling artists.

Editors disagreed over whether the article should clarify that there was no official Richter-scale reading: one asked for that point to be stated, while another argued that a Richter-scale result would be misleading and therefore not useful.

2008.summary: Editors disputed whether the article should identify Atatürk as Muslim: one questioned the evidence and said the available statements might have been made to gain support, while another argued that sources supported describing him as Muslim. They also disagreed over whether to describe his family origin as Albanian or Turkish, with one editor citing sources for an Albanian father and another emphasizing that Atatürk identified as Turkish.

2015.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to move material about Walker’s governorship and political positions into separate articles: one argued that long sections made the biography unwieldy, while others said the material belonged there and a split lacked sufficient justification. They also disputed whether Walker’s “divide and conquer” remark referred to a right-to-work strategy; one editor said sources connected it to that strategy, while others argued it could concern the budget and that any connection should be attributed rather than stated as fact.

2010.summary: Editors disputed whether Vijay-supportive fan sites belonged among the article’s links: one defended them as sites that report his news while acknowledging failed films and citing other outlets, while another said fan sites are generally discouraged as biased, particularly those owned by Galatta.com.

2005.summary: Editors disagreed over how to describe Aesthetic Realism students’ accounts of changing from homosexuality to heterosexuality: one editor favored “statements” as less suggestive of doubt, while another argued the accounts should be presented as claims rather than established fact. They also disputed whether the opening paragraph should include supporters’ response to allegations that the group was a cult; some argued that a rebuttal would make the introduction a back-and-forth debate, while another defended reporting that students called their detractors liars.

2007.summary: Editors disagreed over how much detail the plot summary should include: one wanted an extended account covering the story’s basic information, while others argued it should stick to the main events and leave out extra plot points.

2021.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to describe Shami as a fast or fast-medium bowler: one side pointed to sources classifying him as fast and his reported bowling speed, while the other favored fast-medium based on several sources and questioned whether he still bowled at that speed. They also disagreed over whether to include his appearance in India’s first pink-ball match on home soil, with one editor arguing the occasion mattered and another saying his participation was not notable enough to mention.

Editors disputed whether Shusha’s origins should be described as a town founded in the 1750s by Panah Ali Khan, or whether the site had an earlier Armenian settlement or stronghold; they also disagreed over whether the earlier historical accounts referred to the town or a nearby village.

2026.summary: Editors disputed whether the article should describe human extinction as “possible” or “eventual”; one editor argued for “possible,” saying the cited secondary sources gave probabilities below 100 percent.

2014.summary: Editors disputed changes to the article’s religious-demographic information: one asked for sources for the changes, while the other argued that information used to undo them was old and also lacked references.

2007.summary: Editors disagreed over whether a statement that Ness had appeared in the series “up until now” meant he was out of Brawl: some argued for marking him as excluded, while others said the wording was too unclear and preferred to leave his status uncertain. They also disputed how much space the series article should give non-playable characters, with some defending descriptions of recurring characters and Brawl’s new enemies and others arguing that detailed coverage belonged in the article about Brawl itself.

2021.summary: Editors disagreed over whether baseball and softball count as one discipline or two, and whether freestyle and Greco-Roman wrestling count separately; one editor cited the Olympic programme as grouping baseball and softball while listing the wrestling styles separately.

2014.summary: Editors disputed whether the Dalai Lama’s opposition to Shugden practice should be described as a ban: some supporters treated it as one, while others argued that he lacked the authority to impose a formal ban. They also disagreed over the opening summary, with proposals to describe competing views of Shugden’s nature opposed by calls for a simpler account of what the controversy concerned.

2007.summary: Editors disagreed over how many moves belonged in Melina Perez’s signature-move list: one editor argued that moves used only once or a few times should be removed, while another wanted her finishers and some less-frequent moves retained. They also differed over whether to include moves performed with partners; one editor added several, while others removed the partner-move section because she was not a regular tag-team wrestler.

2024.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the public discussion of Catherine’s absence warranted a separate article or more coverage in her biography; some argued the coverage merited inclusion, while others said it was too early or raised concerns about recent events and privacy. Editors also disputed describing her chemotherapy as “preventative”: some favored the term because it reflected her own wording, while another editor argued it was medically inaccurate and should be quoted or attributed.

2008.summary: Editors disagreed over how prominently to feature Wendy Wu in the opening paragraph: one argued it was a significant part of Song’s career, while another said the roles were already summarized in the career section. They also disagreed about how much detail to include about her career, with one editor objecting to expanded descriptions of minor roles and another defending added detail while agreeing to reduce trivial material.

2006.summary: Editors disagreed over whether Chain of Memories should count as the series’ second title: some said it did, while another characterized it as a bridge between the first and second games, more like “Kingdom Hearts 1.5.”

2010.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the theory should be defined strictly as the claim that Jesus never existed, or also cover views that allow historical people behind some stories or sayings but not as the founder of Christianity. They also disputed whether comparisons to Holocaust denial and other conspiracy claims belonged in the article as examples of scholarly criticism, or were tangential and insulting rather than informative.

2023.summary: Editors disagreed over which form of Markos Botsaris’s name belonged in the infobox’s field for a person’s native name, with some supporting the Albanian form “Marko Boçari.” Another editor questioned whether that modern Albanian spelling was historically appropriate, arguing that Albanian was not then written in that script and proposing a Greek-script form instead.

2010.summary: Editors disagreed over whether character names on the list should match the titles of their individual articles; one argued that the list should use the names people commonly use, and another ultimately agreed.

2011.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the list should classify less-frequent characters as recurring: some supported keeping a recurring-character section with rules for when characters move to the past, while another editor argued that judging character status from appearances was unverifiable inference. They also differed over a proposed one-year cutoff, with one editor preferring the existing approach because recurring characters may be absent for longer.

2014.summary: Editors differed over whether Kurtis should be listed as an extra: one asked whether he belonged on the list, while another argued he should not be included because he would not appear on the show for at least ten weeks.

2015.summary: Editors disagreed over whether Kathy Beale belonged among the present characters after a brief appearance, with some arguing that her return to the list should wait until she resumed a regular role and others saying her first reappearance and a signed regular contract were enough. They also disputed how much family information to include for Lauren’s baby Louie, including whether to add relatives beyond his parents and whether to assign him a surname before it was confirmed.

2017.summary: Editors disagreed over whether Charlie and Matthew should remain on the list after a two-episode return: one view was that they had left again, while others favored keeping them because their story might be revisited. They also differed on whether Libby should be removed as the one-year period ended, with one editor pointing to the actor’s role on another show and others preferring to wait in case of a Christmas or surprise appearance.

2018.summary: Editors disagreed over whether Pam and Charlie, who had made few recent appearances, should remain listed as regular characters or be moved to a less prominent category or removed. They also discussed replacing the list’s one-year period for keeping recurring or guest characters with six months, with some favoring the shorter period and tying removal to the end of a character’s storyline.

2021.summary: Editors disagreed over whether Ian Beale should remain on the current-character list during his extended absence: one argued he had left and should be removed, while another said he had not been confirmed as gone for good. Those favoring removal emphasized that he was not currently appearing and that the actor had said he would not return until 2022 at the earliest; those favoring inclusion described the absence as temporary.

2022.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to list Danielle Harold’s character Lola Pearce as departing: one request said she was leaving, while a response noted that the BBC had not confirmed her exit.

2023.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to combine the current and former character lists: the merger proposal called the split pointless and questioned whether the former-character list was sufficiently supported, while opponents said separate lists help readers navigate the large cast. Editors also disputed whether Will and Janet should be classified as regular characters: one view pointed to their age and long-running appearances, while another argued that age alone did not settle the question and that their appearances remained too occasional.

2006.summary: Editors disagreed over how much space to give Naik’s views and quotations: one called the article an anthology of his thoughts, while another argued it should cover what he says and does. Some editors objected to praise they considered promotional or unsupported, while a supporter complained that achievements were removed as criticism remained.

2012.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the party’s ideology description should reflect its stated Greek nationalism and keep neo-Nazi claims in a separate discussion, or rely on independent sources that classify it as neo-Nazi despite the party’s denial. They also differed over whether the label should appear in the ideology listing without qualification or be marked as disputed.

2007.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to describe the killings as a massacre, an execution, or simply killings, with some favoring “massacre” as a description of mass killing and others preferring “execution” or neutral wording. Those opposing “massacre” argued that it implied cruelty or illegitimacy; opponents of “execution” said that term suggested a lawful judgment and guilt, which they disputed.

2010.summary: One editor argued that the article was not positive enough and restored an older version, while another rejected that approach and urged specific, sourced changes instead.

2021.summary: Editors disagreed over how to define critical race theory in the opening paragraph: one argued it should be described as a framework or theory rather than an academic movement, while others defended the movement-based wording and resisted replacing it with a shorter popular-media definition. They also contested how the article should present academic criticism, including whether older critical arguments belonged in the article and whether a source’s own analysis was enough to label its claims as criticism.

2013.summary: An editor requested that Ali Daei be added to the club’s manager and technical-staff listings, saying he had been appointed head coach.

2011.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to describe Michele Bachmann’s religious worldview as influenced by dominionism: some argued that journalists’ interpretations of her intellectual influences merited inclusion, while others objected that the connection was misleading and proposed wording that attributed the interpretation and noted criticism of it. They also disputed whether her comments about natural disasters should be included, with some calling them a significant, widely reported remark and others describing them as a joke with little lasting relevance.

2005.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the unused, later-flooded buses could be presented as a failure by Nagin: one side cited reports and emergency-plan language, while another argued those sources did not establish his responsibility and pointed to the lack of drivers. They also disputed whether Louisiana’s August 27 request already counted as a request for federal aid or whether the September 2 letter was the first sufficiently specific request, citing competing documents and interpretations of federal law.

2009.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the ending established that Wesker died: some argued that the lava and rockets made his death clear, while others said the game did not confirm his fate. They also disputed whether to call him decapitated, with some favoring a description of the visible events that left readers to decide what happened.

2011.summary: Editors disputed whether three former members should be described as current, inactive, or past members, with one position emphasizing TVXQ’s activities as a duo and another arguing the three should not be removed from the group’s membership while their contracts remained unresolved. The discussion also included an objection that calling the three former members was legally inaccurate before their contracts ended or they left voluntarily.

2009.summary: Editors disagreed over whether and how much to include about the reported assault involving Rihanna, with some arguing that the article should wait for clearer confirmation and historical perspective, while others favored adding a brief, carefully qualified account of the available information. They also disputed whether pop or R&B should be listed first among her musical genres, with proponents of pop pointing to her hits and others arguing that sources supported R&B as her primary genre.

2019.summary: Editors disagreed over whether Rihanna’s Barbadian ambassadorship was an official political role warranting an officeholder box, or an honorary title better left out of that box; one editor argued for including an officeholder box as part of a broader personal profile. They also disputed how much detail belonged in the opening paragraph: one editor favored a shorter overview and removing specifics about her record deal and career achievements, while another wanted to retain the account of how she secured her contract and merge paragraphs.

Editors disagreed over whether to include the Liptak PAL, with one objecting that the cited forum source was unreliable and did not establish that the vehicle was used during the war. The other editor argued that the source described a prototype rejected during the war, supporting its inclusion.

2015.summary: Editors disagreed over whether Cristiano Ronaldo belonged alongside Messi in an opening-paragraph sentence about Messi’s standing and awards: one defended the reference through their rivalry, while another called it misleading. The disagreement also concerned whether the sentence could imply Ronaldo had won four Ballon d’Or awards, and it was reworded after editors raised the clarity problem.

2023.summary: Editors disputed whether Messi should be credited with Barcelona’s 2005 Supercopa de España title: supporters pointed to official club listings, while opponents argued he was not called up for either match and challenged the sources used to credit him. A separate disagreement concerned his 2006 Champions League title, with editors citing conflicting UEFA references over whether to count it and whether to note that he missed the final; arguments also invoked competition rules and other sources.

2020.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include a 2.6-second acceleration time for the Nissan GT-R NISMO: one side said Autocar had measured it, while others argued that the magazine did not identify the figure as an independent test result and might have been repeating manufacturer information.

2007.summary: Editors disputed whether the discography should report worldwide album sales of about 85–86 million or a lower total around 75–76 million, with objections that some higher-total sources were unreliable and arguments that totals could be calculated from country certifications. They also disagreed over U.S. album figures: one editor cited Nielsen SoundScan sales, while another argued that certifications reflect shipments and that club sales should be added to the cited figures.

2022.summary: Editors disputed the number and type of Tejas aircraft represented by the orders, with one arguing that the total included 18 two-seat trainers and another challenging that count and the sourcing for it.

2015.summary: Editors disputed whether Albania should be listed as an Allied state, with some arguing it fought alongside Axis Italy while others pointed to its resistance against Axis forces and its postwar treaty status. Those opposing inclusion said resistance by Albanian groups and participation in a postwar treaty did not establish that Albania as a state had joined the Allies during the war; supporters argued that occupation, resistance, and treaty recognition justified its inclusion.

2007.summary: Editors disagreed over how to identify Bumblebee’s newer Camaro: one argued that the scene made it a road-going prototype rather than a concept car, while others said the available evidence did not establish a specific version and favored calling it a Camaro or fifth-generation Camaro.

2009.summary: Editors disputed whether criticism of Levin—including Media Matters reports and comments by David Frum—belonged in his biography: opponents called it predictable, weakly sourced opinion that lacked wider significance, while supporters argued that published criticism by notable commentators could be reported as opinion. They also debated presentation, with proposals to shorten the material and integrate it into the account of his radio show rather than maintain a lengthy standalone criticism section.

2005.summary: Editors disagreed over how much plot detail belonged in the article: some wanted to replace the chapter-by-chapter account with a brief overview, while others praised the detailed summaries. After the article was shortened, one editor argued that the remaining synopsis was too brief and misleading, while another defended a shorter account and asked what length would be appropriate.

2008.summary: Editors disputed whether Vista and Windows XP sales figures could be compared fairly, with one arguing that the figures used different channels and periods and therefore could not support the article’s conclusions. Another editor questioned whether preinstalled copies counted as sales and said that purchases or reuse of existing XP copies also made sales figures a poor measure of how many people used each system.

Editors disagreed over how specifically to describe Niko Bellic’s national background: several cited sources calling him Serbian, while another argued the article should say only that he was from the former Yugoslavia because more specific claims were speculation.

2016.summary: Editors disagreed over whether “Habesha” and “Abyssinian” should describe narrowly defined groups or allow broader, context-dependent meanings; one contributor also cautioned that the terms should not automatically be treated as equivalent.

2005.summary: Editors disputed how much space the article’s criticism section should take and whether to organize it around individual critics or summarize the claims more briefly. Some argued that describing the criticism and its context was part of the story, while others said extensive quotations and individual subheadings risked giving accusations too much weight.
