2016.summary: Editors disagreed over which songs to name in George Michael’s entry: one argued that his solo hit “Faith” should replace one of three Wham! songs, while another defended the Wham! selections as better known. The discussion broadened into disagreement over whether entries should be limited to three career credits and whether that limit should allow exceptions for people notable in several fields.

2017.summary: Editors disputed whether the article should call the film an international co-production involving the Netherlands, the UK, France and the US: supporters cited sources listing those countries, while an opponent argued the sources did not establish that description. The disagreement also concerned whether the sources justified describing countries as producers; one editor said they identified production companies from those countries, while another argued that companies, not countries, produced the film and suggested more qualified wording.

2020.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to retain the candidates’ detailed platform table: one argued it was too long and could be incomplete or uneven, favoring a shorter summary of a few policies for each candidate. Another argued that the full table offered an organized overview and that selecting only “main” policies would be subjective.

2016.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to separate criticism of the alt-right from the article’s account of its beliefs: one editor argued that the article relied mainly on critics’ opinions and should distinguish criticism from description, while also proposing separate sections to address perceived bias. Other editors objected that isolating criticism would make the article less neutral and argued that the article should follow reliable sources rather than add positive material simply to balance negative coverage.

2018.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the article should describe the alt-right as “somewhat ill-defined.” One argued that its varied and sometimes conflicting beliefs do not add up to a definition, while another maintained that the article’s list of beliefs clearly describes the movement.

2017.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to create a separate page for episode listings during the show’s second season, with proponents pointing to the growing number of episodes and the prospect of a more crowded main article. Opponents argued that the existing list was not yet long enough to justify a split and that it should wait until the article became impractical to read or maintain.

2016.summary: Editors disputed whether the season article should include the earlier Polish and British air dates for four episodes; one editor argued that these were legitimate broadcasts and should be recorded alongside the U.S. dates. Another editor argued that “original air date” referred to the original network’s broadcasts and asked for reliable sources to support the dates.

2021.summary: Editors disputed whether to describe the film as a “standalone sequel”: one objected that its producer had said it was not a sequel and proposed calling it a standalone version, while others argued the label described its connection to the earlier film. They also disagreed over how much opening action to include in the plot summary, including the first team’s deaths and Harley Quinn’s capture; one side wanted those details and their chronology clarified, while another argued that naming minor characters and recounting the sequence added unnecessary detail.

2016.summary: Editors disagreed over whether episode 605 should be titled “Diamond in the Rough” or “Street Rats”: listings gave the former, while the show’s creator said the latter was correct, and editors differed over which source to follow. One participant urged waiting for an official press release, while another argued newer sources supported restoring “Street Rats.”

2019.summary: Editors disagreed over how much detail to retain in the article’s storyline summaries: some favored keeping explanations and context, while others argued for tighter summaries and cutting details they considered unnecessary. They also debated whether a strict word-count target was too limiting, with one editor saying needed details had been removed and another emphasizing concision and the article’s length.

2016.summary: Editors disagreed over whether Azerbaijani forces had gained and held heights near Talysh and Lalatepe: some argued that videos and reports supported describing gains, while others disputed the evidence and cited reporting that forces had been pushed back behind the line of contact.

Editors disputed whether Charlotte’s title history should be described as one continuous reign, after a televised comment counted her time holding two titles together as 309 days. Some editors proposed acknowledging that count, while others argued that the announcer’s comment was not a reliable source and that the official histories treated the titles as separate.

2017.summary: Editors disputed how the article should describe Sarsour’s views on sharia: one argued that she should be identified as an advocate, citing sources that used that label, while others said the article could describe her personal religious practice and comments but should not imply that she supported imposing Islamic law as civil law.

2016.summary: Editors disagreed over whether players who left during the season should stay in the squad statistics table or be listed separately. Those favoring separate listing said players no longer at the club should be identified to avoid confusing readers, while another editor argued that players who were in the squad when the season began should remain and that the page’s existing section on departures was sufficient.

2018.summary: Editors disputed whether the VidCon incident involving Benjamin’s attendance at Anita Sarkeesian’s panel should be described as part of a targeted harassment campaign or framed more cautiously, with some arguing the characterization overstated what sources established about his intent and others defending it as supported by reporting. They also disputed how to characterize Benjamin politically, including whether he should be labeled alt-right or far-right and how much weight to give his own rejection of those labels compared with outside descriptions.

2019.summary: Editors disputed how the article should describe Benjamin’s comments about Labour MP Jess Phillips: some wanted the opening paragraph to identify the comments and note that he called them jokes, while another editor argued that the wording omitted context and misrepresented the remarks as threats. They also disagreed over how much detail this controversy deserved in the opening paragraph, with some favoring a fuller account and others preferring a brief mention that directed readers to the article’s main text.

2016.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the article should include US and Russian officials’ speculation about the cause of the flight’s disappearance. Some argued that widely reported officials’ views belonged in the account even though their basis was unknown, while others called the claims unsupported and said reports that no signs of an explosion had been detected should also be reflected.

Editors disagreed over whether to call one team “Team SmackDown Live” or use a shorter form, and whether to identify elimination matches as men’s or women’s matches; they also disputed including managers in the match listings. They differed on whether to add “traditional” to match descriptions, while one editor argued that match order should remain unchanged until the event established it.

Editors disagreed over whether the opening paragraph should directly call the shooting a terrorist attack: some supported the label based on its use by news and government sources, while others argued that the motive was not established. Some preferred describing the attack as widely characterized as terrorism, while others considered that wording too cautious or said the first sentence should state only the basic facts and leave interpretation for later.

2017.summary: Editors questioned whether Lionsgate should be identified as a production company, since its film-credit listing and description as a presenting company did not clearly establish that it helped make the film. One editor argued that these references reflected distribution rather than production and concluded Lionsgate should not be listed as a producer.

Editors disagreed over whether to include Stephen Miller’s rebuke of CNN reporter Jim Acosta after an exchange about immigration, and whether to quote Miller directly or summarize the exchange with more context. Some argued that the quote was Miller’s own framing and did not belong in the article, while others considered the exchange significant enough to include; another editor objected that the episode gave undue weight to Miller’s opinion about Acosta.

2019.summary: Editors disagreed over how to label criticism of Omar’s remarks: some favored headings referring to allegations of antisemitism or the use of antisemitic tropes, while others argued that such labels could conflate criticism of her comments with claims about Omar herself. They also disagreed over whether the controversy belonged in the opening paragraph, with some arguing it merited inclusion and others preferring to keep criticism and responses in the article body.

2017.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include a controversy section about Paul Abrahamian’s reported plan, with some calling the wording biased and unsupported while others argued the events were controversial and offered media coverage as sources. They also disputed whether the proposed outlets were reliable enough; one editor rejected the listed sources and said the section should be removed unless credible sources could be found.

2016.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the article’s infobox should present the Free Syrian Army as a unified force taking part in the operation or as a broad label used by separate rebel groups. Some argued that groups identifying with the Free Syrian Army should be listed under that name, while others said this would wrongly suggest a single organization or command structure.

2017.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include information about the soundtrack’s release before the game launched: one argued that available independent coverage amounted only to announcements and track listings, while another defended adding the information and questioned why a restriction on predicting future events applied.

2018.summary: Editors disagreed over how the opening paragraph should describe Gab: one proposal sought to present it as a free-speech service as well as a platform associated with the alt-right, while others argued that this framing misrepresented the sources and created false balance. They also disputed whether the paragraph should call Gab “known for” its far-right user base; one editor said the cited sources did not support that wording, while others defended it as reflecting coverage of the site.

2019.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the opening paragraph should describe Gab’s free-speech policy alongside its mainly far-right userbase. Supporters argued that the policy was important to understanding the site, while opponents said independent coverage focused more on its far-right users and did not justify presenting the policy as a defining feature.

2017.summary: Editors disagreed over whether contestant tables should distinguish safe contestants who received favorable or unfavorable critiques, including by using different colors, or simply mark them all as safe; opponents argued that this would classify performances through editors’ interpretation rather than explicit results. Some editors argued that published episode reviews could support identifying high and low performers, while others maintained that such classifications were not sufficiently explicit for the table.

Editors disagreed about when to replace Japanese names with English ones: one view was to wait until an episode had fully aired in English, while a request sought the change several days beforehand, with a commenter arguing the names were already official.

Editors disputed which height to list for Miss Bolivia: one argued that the pageant’s contestant profile might be wrong and sought to change its figure, while another said the proposed alternative lacked a source and favored showing sourced conflicting measurements for readers to assess.

2018.summary: Editors disputed whether the film’s production budget should be listed as $250 million or as a range, after a report put it above $300 million; one comment also raised the possibility that figures included costs beyond production. A separate discussion questioned the opening paragraph’s budget and reported losses, pointing to figures that differed from the information box and sources that did not directly support the stated loss estimate.

2017.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the article should have a separate section on Trump’s authoritarian tendencies: supporters argued that the subject was widely covered in reliable sources, while critics said the section’s content and presentation were not neutral and should be removed. Some editors also objected that the section’s title made a strong judgment and that its examples relied on opinions or did not clearly support the claim; others argued that the sourced material warranted inclusion.

2024.summary: Editors disagreed over how to order the actors named in the article’s infobox: some argued it should follow the film’s on-screen credits, while another argued it should use the poster’s billing block, a shorter list of billed actors. They also debated whether the opening paragraph should summarize the critical response, and how to describe accounts that characterized the film as well received versus more divisive without presenting one overall verdict.

2021.summary: Editors disagreed about whether Thomas Haden Church and Rhys Ifans belonged in the cast list: some said sources confirmed the characters but not that those actors appeared, while others argued that entertainment coverage identifying the characters by those actors was enough to include them. The disagreement centered on whether the available reporting established the actors’ involvement, rather than only the return of their characters.

2022.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the plot summary should clarify that “Peter-Two” and “Peter-Three” are nicknames, with one editor arguing readers could mistake them for actual names and others considering the clarification unnecessary or better suited to a footnote. They also disputed whether to add details about which universes the characters came from, with some editors saying this information was not needed to understand the summary and another arguing it helped identify the characters.

2018.summary: Editors disagreed over how to define a “major candidate”: one argued that candidates should meet a five-poll threshold, while others supported counting major media coverage as a basis for inclusion. Another proposed standard treated holding certain public offices as sufficient, but editors questioned whether that should include state legislators and similar officials.

2019.summary: Editors disagreed over whether Andrew Yang and Marianne Williamson belonged in the article’s “major candidates” group: some argued that news coverage treated them like other major contenders, while others favored a five-poll threshold that they had not both met. Other proposals included using debate qualification or substantial campaign coverage, but editors questioned whether such coverage-based standards were clear and consistently applicable.

2017.summary: Editors requested corrections to the match listing, including replacing Bray Wyatt with Braun Strowman and identifying Seth Rollins, rather than Dean Ambrose, as the wrestler Sheamus pinned to win the Raw Tag Team titles.

Editors disputed whether career foreign-service officers appointed as ambassadors belonged in the article. Some argued the list focused on political appointments, not career-service promotions; others said its stated definition of political appointments included ambassadors and other foreign-service officers appointed by the president.

2022.summary: Editors disagreed over how much space a widely covered video from the general-election campaign should receive, with some arguing its coverage made it a defining campaign event and others saying it was not important enough to include or deserved only brief mention. They also disputed whether the video merited a separate section, rather than a shorter reference within broader campaign coverage.

2020.summary: Editors disagreed over how to describe the game’s critical reception: some argued that Metacritic’s “universal acclaim” summary should be reported, while others said notable critical reviews were more mixed and raised problems with relying on the aggregate score alone. They also disputed whether the article’s opening summary should characterize reactions to the story and themes as divided, with one position favoring a concise account of praise and criticism and another warning that such wording overstated dissenting reviews.

2017.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the opening should state that Russian interference occurred, or frame it as an allegation and attribute the conclusion to U.S. intelligence agencies. They also disputed whether to include criticism that a public intelligence report offered little evidence: supporters called that criticism relevant, while opponents said it was outdated or deserved too little weight.

Editors disagreed over whether Carlos Sainz should remain listed with Toro Rosso on the basis of an earlier report describing his contract, or whether newer reports of a Renault move justified leaving the seat unconfirmed; some editors rejected those reports because they relied on unnamed sources, while others argued that reliable publications could be cited for their claims. A separate dispute concerned whether proposed safety and technical rule changes, including the halo, belonged in the article before formal approval: some editors supported including sourced proposals if clearly labelled as proposals, while others argued they should wait until ratified.

2018.summary: Editors disagreed over whether Racing Point Force India should be shown as a separate constructor from the excluded Sahara Force India, and whether the two should have separate rows in the championship tables. They also differed over whether the new entry warranted its own article immediately or whether its history should remain in the existing Force India article until the situation became clearer.

2017.summary: Editors discussed what to list in the couples table as Debbie McGee’s “known for” description, with one editor suggesting wording from a BBC profile that called her a television personality, presenter and the late Paul Daniels’s wife. Other editors said she should be identified as a magician’s assistant, arguing that this was how most people knew her and that the article should not simply follow the BBC’s publicity wording.

Editors disagreed over whether the article’s title should call the subject a “myth” or a “controversy”: one editor proposed a new title, while others argued that “controversy” would give too much weight to the claim that Irish people were slaves. They also disputed whether to include brief academic remarks suggesting that some Irish people were slaves; opponents said the remarks were too limited to represent a meaningful scholarly debate, while a supporter argued they showed that some academics held that view.

2022.summary: Editors disagreed over how to label Mondaire Jones in the New York district table: some argued he should be listed as an incumbent in the district where he was running, even though he represented another district. Others said he should not be called an incumbent there because the new district included none of his old district, and argued that describing his move as redistricting would be inaccurate.

2018.summary: Editors disagreed over which promotional poster to use: one favored replacing the original with the newest release, while another said that when posters appeared at roughly the same time, the first uploaded could remain unless editors discussed a change. They also differed on how prominently the opening paragraph should describe the season as a crossover: one editor sought to emphasize its landmark status, while another supported a concise, sourced mention and questioned claims that it was highly anticipated or unprecedented.

Editors disagreed over whether the article should list Sheamus’s time in the Royal Rumble as two seconds or retain the official statistics page’s 20-second figure, with some arguing that other statements supported two seconds. An opposing concern was that different sources might count time in the match differently, so the article should use a consistent method rather than combine figures from sources with possibly different criteria.

2021.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to describe Rodrigo as a “singer-songwriter” or as a singer and songwriter: some argued that the hyphenated label was supported by numerous publications, while others said it implied a particular kind of songwriting that she had not yet established. They also disputed whether repeated year labels in the discography table should be merged into single cells, with proponents calling that tidier and opponents raising concerns about readability and accessibility.

2017.summary: A contributor proposed noting that three songs were performed only on the first night in a city, after observing that they were missing from a later Philadelphia show. Another editor favored one general set list with a note that it might not represent every date, while a further reply questioned the reliability of the set-list source cited for the proposal.

2018.summary: Editors disputed whether Wagner should be identified as American based on the country he played for at senior level, and whether nationality flags should appear in the article at all.

2025.summary: Editors disputed whether the opening paragraph should describe Kirk as “far-right,” “right-wing,” or “conservative”: one argued that “far-right” better matched the sources and article, while others preferred “conservative,” saying that term appeared more often in the article and its sources.

2020.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the women’s championship matches belonged in a section for world-title matches: one editor objected to treating them as world titles without evidence, while another cited WWE descriptions that called them world championships. They also disputed whether brief 24/7 title changes should appear in the match table, with one editor favoring their inclusion as title changes and others saying they were segments, not matches.

2016.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the article should call the Universal Championship a world title: some cited wrestling and news sources that used that description, while others argued that WWE had not designated it as one. The disagreement also turned on whether the title’s stated standing alongside, or intended importance beyond, WWE’s other championship was enough to support that label.

2019.summary: Editors disputed whether the episode summary should say the Dothraki were nearly wiped out in their initial charge: one objected that many later appeared in the attack on King’s Landing, while another argued that the wording described the charge, not the entire battle.

2017.summary: One editor argued that the season’s ratings entries left out low episode figures and urged adding them, while another said figures available only in comment sections were not reliable sources.

2018.summary: One editor asked whether the United Kingdom, United States and Israel should be included, while another argued that they did not qualify because they allow free elections and speech and lack an all-pervasive ideology or government.

2017.summary: Editors disagreed over whether reported transfer fees should be listed when the club had not disclosed them: one argued they were important and could be labeled as press reports, while another questioned how their accuracy could be verified and objected to relying on sources considered unreliable for football coverage.
Editors disputed describing Chanelle’s actions as “justified”: one objected that this was an opinion and said she had been spoken to after throwing a cup on the floor.

2019.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to show the Scottish National Party and Plaid Cymru as separate entries in national polling tables or combine their results with “others”; those favoring removal cited how pollsters reported the figures and the greater usefulness of regional polling, while opponents argued that the parties’ national support and parliamentary representation warranted separate entries. The debate also considered whether party representation or poll coverage should guide table inclusion, with some arguing that other countries’ polling tables show there is room for more entries and others insisting that inclusion should follow how polling sources report results.

2017.summary: Editors questioned whether the film’s official title was “Dark Phoenix” rather than “X-Men: Dark Phoenix,” and a source from the producer was offered in support of the shorter title.

Editors disagreed over whether the opening paragraph repeated details about iOS 11’s features and critical reception, with one editor seeking to cut or condense material and another arguing that descriptions of features and reviews served different purposes. They also disputed whether calling the iPad changes a “revolution” was justified: one editor questioned the word because no review used it, while another defended it as a summary of reviews describing a transformed experience.

Editors disagreed over whether the article should be titled as a terrorist attack, with some arguing that reports and police statements supported that label and others saying it was too early to classify the event that way; proposals instead included descriptive titles referring to an explosion or bombing, and the article was moved to “2017 Manchester Arena bombing.”

2020.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to classify the system as Cyclone Gati before an official bulletin was issued: one said satellite bulletin data already showed an upgrade, while another urged waiting for the latest bulletin from India’s official regional center.

2017.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the article’s background should discuss the nearby mosque’s past links to radical preachers and militants. Supporters said that history was widely reported in coverage of the attack and belonged as context, while opponents argued that the mosque’s role in the attack was unclear and that including its past risked blaming the victims.

2018.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to mention “Bcash” as another name for Bitcoin Cash: some considered it a pejorative term, while another view treated it as an informal shortening that was not inherently negative. One proposal was to include the term but explain that its use is disfavored in some contexts, rather than present it as an ordinary alternative name.

2017.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the car incident should be described as an attack or in terms that did not imply intent. Some pointed to witness accounts and news descriptions as support for calling it an attack, while others argued that editors should not infer intent from appearances or video and urged neutral wording while the driver’s case was unresolved. One proposed approach was to report that some media and witnesses called it an attack, alongside the fact that charges had been filed, without making a judgment about the driver’s guilt.

Editors disputed how to present experts’ reactions to the memo: one argued that repetitive quotations made the scientific-reaction section confusing and should be condensed and organized, while a reply cautioned against editors declaring a scientific consensus themselves. They also disagreed over whether to include a poll of Google employees about Damore’s firing, with supporters citing its media coverage and opponents questioning its sampling and whether it deserved space in the article.

2019.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the opening paragraph should present violence as a principal feature of antifa, with some seeking stronger emphasis and others opposing that framing. Opponents noted that violence was already mentioned and argued that presenting it as central overgeneralized across a movement whose cited state assessment said most members did not promote or endorse violence.

2017.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the article should have a separate section on environmental factors, including climate change: supporters argued that Irma-related coverage warranted it, while opponents said broader factors belonged in general or season-level articles and storm-specific conditions could go in the meteorological history. They also disputed whether discussing climate-related phenomena risked implying a causal link to Irma; supporters said the section could describe the phenomena without making that inference, while opponents argued the article should not suggest a connection unsupported by storm-specific evidence.

2019.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include a footnote explaining why fuel regulations specify fuel amounts by weight rather than volume, alongside the season’s increase in the maximum permitted fuel amount. Supporters said the explanation helped readers understand the regulations, while opponents argued that measuring fuel by weight was not new that year and that the uncited explanation was unnecessary in an article about the sporting season.

2018.summary: Editors disagreed over how to present Puerto Rico’s figure of 2,975 deaths: some wanted it described as an estimate, while others opposed adding that qualification to the government-adopted total. One editor argued that the figure could be off by hundreds or thousands and that its precise form could be misleading.

Editors disagreed on whether Ben’s departure should be described as quitting or self-elimination: some argued she left outside the competition’s formal elimination choices, while others said she left through that week’s elimination process and favored terminology used by reporting sources. Editors also disputed Thorgy’s first-episode placement: some argued that positive critiques meant she should be marked as high, while others pointed to conflicting source descriptions and favored marking her safe rather than relying on editors’ interpretations.

2022.summary: Editors disagreed over whether polls from before August 5 should be hidden by default: one objected that all 2022 polls should remain visible, while another defended the display choice as a way to make the article easier to read and said the polls remained accessible by clicking to show them.

2018.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the opening-paragraph description of reviews as generally negative was supported: some argued review-site summaries justified it, while others said aggregator labels or combining differing reports could not establish a critical consensus.

Editors disagreed over whether the article could describe Somatemps and its links to Societat Civil Catalana as far-right: one side said media sources supported the characterization, while another questioned the evidence and the label. One editor proposed attributing claims about the links to the researcher who reported them rather than stating them as established facts.

An editor challenged listing Armenia and Serbia as expected participants, arguing the cited sources did not establish that either would compete, and questioned an infobox link to an article that did not yet exist.

Editors disputed whether the mural discussed in the article should be called antisemitic outright or described with qualifying wording, with some favoring “widely condemned as antisemitic” and others arguing for “allegedly antisemitic.” They also disagreed over whether surveys of Labour supporters, rather than party members, belonged in an article about antisemitism within the party.

Editors disagreed over whether the season page should follow the layout of earlier seasons or use names for competition rounds that matched the show’s terminology, such as “Top 24” instead of “semifinalists.” One editor also argued for changing the tables to improve accessibility, while another wanted the page to remain more like earlier season pages.

Editors disagreed over whether to rename the transaction a proposed merger, as one proposal argued, or retain the proposed acquisition wording. An opponent argued that the transaction’s complicated legal structure and the resulting company’s control and ownership made “acquisition” the more accurate description and “merger” potentially misleading.
Editors disagreed over whether the article should list only full-length albums or also singles that charted on the Gaon Albums chart.

2022.summary: Editors disagreed over whether a tropical depression observed on September 25 was the same system later identified as Tropical Depression Luis: one raised the possibility, while another said the available weather records indicated they were separate systems.

2020.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the results summary should show only the final round of caucus voting or also the first-round vote totals, with some arguing that the extra figures were useful and others that they did not determine the outcome or made the summary too crowded. They also disputed whether to report 13 or 14 national delegates for Buttigieg: the party’s results showed 14, while the cited New York Times and Des Moines Register counts showed 13, and editors questioned whether the count should remain provisional while a recount was pending.

2018.summary: Editors disagreed over whether a suicide bombing during the campaign merited its own section or only a brief mention; one editor called it a major event, while another argued it was not significant enough for a separate section. They also disagreed over whether the operation should be described as ongoing or as completed, with one position distinguishing the main fighting from later insurgent attacks and the other citing continuing fighting and official statements that the operation continued.

Editors disagreed over whether to describe alleged Russian bot activity in the #ReleaseTheMemo campaign as a meaningful part of the memo’s story: some argued it belonged in the article, while others said its impact was unknown and the connection to the memo had faded. They also disputed whether this issue merited mention in the opening paragraph, with some favoring inclusion and others arguing it was no longer prominent enough.

Editors disagreed over whether the article should include a section about Catalonia and the Eurovision contest. One editor argued the cited source did not support claims that Catalonia’s broadcaster would seek membership in the European Broadcasting Union or was actively trying to enter; others favored keeping the section as useful context and pointed to other places listed despite not being independent states.

2019.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the contest’s high ticket prices belonged in the article: some argued they were criticism worth covering, while others said expensive tickets were not an incident and should be left out of that section. They also debated whether the temporary suspension of ticket sales over reported irregularities was a separate incident, with some supporting its inclusion and others describing it as minor.

2018.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to list the victims’ names and ages: opponents said the list added little to readers’ understanding and risked turning the article into a memorial, while supporters said it was relevant to an event with a small number of deaths. They also disputed a photograph of the suspect’s arrest, with supporters arguing it illustrated a significant event and showed details not conveyed by text, while opponents considered the arrest routine and the image lacking useful information.

2023.summary: Editors disputed whether the article should report that sources describe Milei as far-right, with some arguing the label misrepresents him without deeper analysis and others saying it should be included when attributed to reliable sources. The disagreement also concerned whether listing the label alongside other descriptions adequately represented competing views, or whether its prominence risked presenting a contested characterization as the article’s own judgment.

2025.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to keep a section about Milei’s book-launch performance: one argued the event was not significant to Argentine politics or informative about Milei, while another said coverage focused on his conduct as president and its effect on his public image. A further objection was that the section gave too much space to a single event and relied heavily on social-media posts and celebrity opinions.

2018.summary: Editors disagreed over whether each episode should be described as 60 minutes long or as a shorter program once commercial breaks were excluded; one editor cited the running time shown by download services, while another challenged that reasoning.

2019.summary: Editors disagreed over how to classify contestants in team challenges: one view was that only contestants singled out for praise should be marked as receiving high critiques, while another treated membership on the winning team or positive comments as grounds for different placement labels. They also disputed whether contestants described as safe in the episode should instead receive high or low labels, with some arguing those labels reflected the performances and others insisting the table should follow the episode’s explicit safe declarations.

2025.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to mention Sweeney’s reported Republican registration: some argued it belonged in coverage of the jeans-ad controversy, while others said registration alone did not establish a public political affiliation worth including. Even among those favoring inclusion, there was disagreement over placement, with some supporting a brief mention alongside the controversy but opposing an infobox label.

2019.summary: Editors disagreed over how much background about real people and events belonged in the film article: some said the character descriptions contained too much detail that was not relevant to the film. Another editor argued that historical connections helped explain how the film referenced real events and people, while also agreeing to shorten or move some material.

Editors disagreed over which company or division to name as the show’s producer: proposals included Nickelodeon Productions and Nickelodeon Animation Studio, while others argued that the available press release and episode credits supported naming Nickelodeon or waiting for more direct evidence.

2018.summary: Editors disputed how to describe the suspected perpetrators in the article’s infobox: some favored naming Russian state actors or GRU agents based on reporting and official accusations, while another argued the field should be omitted until police named suspects. They also disagreed over whether Russian accusations against British or other intelligence services should be listed alongside Russia, with some seeing that as necessary and others warning it would give unsupported alternatives too much prominence.

Editors disputed whether Polish railway employees working for the German-run railway in occupied Poland should be described as collaborators, given their role in operating trains used for deportations and military transport. Supporters argued that sources connected Polish railway personnel with collaboration, while opponents said the cited material described the German railway organization rather than the workers and stressed that many workers were forced to serve.

2020.summary: Editors disagreed over whether Benjamin Netanyahu belonged on the endorsements list because a report said he was eager for Trump to win a second term: some considered that support equivalent to an endorsement. Others argued that wanting Trump to win was not enough without a public statement of support from Netanyahu.

2021.summary: Editors disagreed about how to organize the article’s awards table: one preferred listing awards by year, while another opposed a years-first format and favored organizing the information so readers could see how many awards the artist received in each category.

2018.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include journalist Robert Fisk’s report that people he spoke with in Douma said they had not heard of a gas attack, and how much weight that account deserved. Supporters argued that Fisk’s report had received substantial coverage and should be presented alongside criticism; opponents questioned its evidentiary basis and warned against giving a minority account equal standing with other reporting.

2023.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include Invest 93L in the season’s storm list before it became a tropical cyclone: one argued its media attention and Florida emergency declaration justified inclusion, while others said it did not qualify until it developed further. They also disputed whether Tropical Storm Harold warranted a separate article; one editor argued its coverage and impacts supported one, while another said a separate page was unnecessary once its material had been expanded beyond the season article’s account.

2019.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the tournament tables should use national flag icons: supporters said they help readers identify competitors’ nationalities, while opponents argued the icons should be removed or accompanied by country names under the site’s style guidance.

2022.summary: Editors disagreed over how to present the event’s disputed attendance figures: one favored placing the reported numbers in the infobox as the actual figures, while another argued that both should remain identified as claims rather than treating either as settled.

2023.summary: Editors disputed whether the article could state that Vince McMahon had no role in booking WrestleMania 39: some argued that available sources described him as uninvolved in creative, while others objected that his behind-the-scenes input could not be ruled out without a direct source.

2018.summary: Editors disputed whether the album would arrive on July 20 or in August, with conflicting reports and statements by Ariana Grande cited in support of each date; they also disagreed over whether a song due July 20 was a single or a promotional release.

2022.summary: Editors questioned whether a Disney-focused blog was reliable enough for the list’s citations, and another editor agreed it was not, replacing its citations with sources from industry publications. They also disagreed over whether shows unavailable in some countries for reasons other than censorship should be classified as regional or global originals, with one editor noting that assessing availability across all markets could make regional classifications incomplete or arbitrary.

2023.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to mark “Willow” as ended after it was removed from Disney+: some treated the showrunner’s past-tense tweet as evidence it was over, while others said the tweet did not explicitly say the show was canceled and pointed to his earlier description of a hiatus.

2020.summary: Editors disagreed over whether Lance Stroll should be listed as a 2021 driver: some considered team-principal comments and other reporting sufficient evidence, while others wanted a fresh official confirmation, arguing that the team’s contract situation had changed and reports might be based on assumptions.

2021.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include senior team personnel departures in the season’s team-changes section: some argued that changes in leadership matter to teams, while others said personnel belong in team or individual articles rather than a section about championship entries. They also debated whether to mention that Aston Martin and Mercedes shared safety-car duties, with some favoring a brief reference and others arguing the change was commercial detail better suited to articles about safety cars or teams.

2018.summary: Editors disagreed about whether the article should cover involuntary celibacy as a broader social experience, which some said academic sources discussed beyond online communities, or focus on the online incel subculture, which others considered the article’s central subject. They also disputed whether killers belonged in the article when sources linked them to celibacy but not clearly to the subculture; some editors considered that connection too speculative, while another argued that a person’s own statement of involuntary celibacy could qualify.

2023.summary: Editors disputed whether a large expansion translated from the French article belonged in the biography, with critics arguing it included too many minor details and material they considered non-neutral or self-serving. The editor defending the additions said they were checked against sources and argued that specific passages should be assessed individually rather than removing the expanded content wholesale.

2019.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to list countries as withdrawn when they were missing from a video but not confirmed as withdrawing by a reliable published source; some relied on the video, while others urged waiting for stronger confirmation. They also disputed removing a notes section that included country debuts and possible withdrawals: one editor objected that some sourced information was omitted, while another argued the list format encouraged disruptive editing and that the withdrawals remained unconfirmed.

Editors disputed whether to give the film a single $55 million production budget, which one position argued was supported by Box Office Mojo, or to show a wider range reflecting estimates from multiple sources.

Editors disagreed over whether the article should describe Jung Kook as BTS’s “main vocalist”: supporters pointed to media and company-produced material using the title, while other editors questioned whether sources supported it and argued that such role labels were unclear and potentially misleading to readers.

2021.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to record Hurricane Sam’s peak at 135 knots based on the National Hurricane Center’s uncertain estimate, or retain the lower, more firmly confirmed figure. They also debated whether Sam’s long meteorological history justified its own article: supporters said the season section was already too long and omitted important details, while others argued it could be shortened and questioned the need for a separate page.

2022.summary: Editors disagreed over what the season’s “strongest storm” should mean: one argued for comparing maximum wind speeds, which favored Ian, while others used minimum air pressure, which favored Fiona. They also debated whether seasonal track maps should use maps published by the National Hurricane Center or maps made from best-track data; supporters of the former cited the built-in key, while supporters of the latter stressed broader coverage and quicker updates.

2021.summary: Editors disagreed over when to publish the Hurricane Olaf draft: one questioned why storm drafts remained unpublished, while another said Olaf had enough material to be published and that review could delay articles unnecessarily. They also disagreed over Enrique and Nora, with one favoring publication given their impacts and another saying Enrique needed substantial expansion first.

2022.summary: Editors disagreed over whether Hurricane Kay warranted a separate article: some argued its effects on land justified one, while another questioned whether its history could be covered adequately in the season article. The discussion also raised whether Kay’s Southern California impacts provided enough additional material for a standalone account. coverage_note

2020.summary: Editors disagreed over whether reports about a new character replacing Batwoman should be included when the coverage appeared to trace back to a deleted Reddit screenshot; some favored including the reports with attribution, while others questioned their sourcing. They also differed over where to place industry commentary about the casting news, with one editor calling it too extensive for the casting section and another supporting its placement there until more analysis was available.

2019.summary: Editors disputed whether Monet and Monique should be listed as receiving high placements or as safe after their critiques: one editor argued all three contestants announced safe together should be listed as safe, while another editor’s source was interpreted as distinguishing Monet and Monique as high and Manila as safe.

2018.summary: Editors disagreed over which sources to use for the album’s production credits, as published credit lists differed about who produced particular tracks. One position favored relying on multiple independent music publications where their accounts agreed; the other favored Tidal’s digital credits, arguing that those publications relied on incomplete Spotify listings.

2024.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the election summary box should list PTI-backed independent candidates as a separate group, with some arguing that this reflected how news sources described them and others favoring the official classification of candidates as independents or warning that their affiliations were unclear. They also disputed whether to include allegations of military involvement in election rigging: some editors pointed to extensive reporting, while others argued that the sources were speculative or did not provide enough supporting evidence.

2023.summary: Editors discussed restricting changes to the article after repeated vandalism, and a reply noted that the page had been semi-protected.

2024.summary: Editors disagreed over whether Hurricane Kirk merited a separate article: some argued its European impacts justified one, while others said its tropical-cyclone history alone did not and debated whether any article should describe it as a hurricane or a European windstorm. They also questioned whether the season could be called the second-costliest without a source explicitly making that comparison, with one editor arguing that adding separate storm-damage estimates would not establish the ranking.

2020.summary: Editors disagreed over whether “911” should be described as a single, with one questioning reports that it was the next single because they said the artist or her label had not confirmed it, while another argued that publications identifying it as a single were sufficient evidence. They also differed over whether radio airplay or an official radio release was needed to establish a song’s single status.

2024.summary: Editors disagreed over how to describe Imran Khan’s allegations concerning Munir and Khan’s wife: one wanted the article to distinguish between concerns about her safety and blame for her imprisonment, while others argued the accusation was unsupported or did not need repeating. They also disputed whether to include claims linking Munir to pressure on a businessman and reported extortion, with objections about the sources and relevance countered by an editor who said the matters were reported and related to his role.

2019.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to list “Spyfall” as one story or as two separate episodes, debating whether its announced two-part format and differing directors justified treating the parts separately.

Editors disagreed about which year the film’s events should be placed in, citing conflicting clues from the films and related promotional material; proposed dates included 1967, 1970 and 1972. Some suggested removing the year from the plot description to avoid the inconsistency, while others argued for retaining dates, and the discussion records a decision to keep the years in the plot on this page.

Editors disagreed over whether Tamil should be listed as a language in which Saaho was made: some argued that only portions were filmed in Tamil and it should not be listed as a full filming language, while others pointed to the producers’ and cast members’ descriptions of the film as trilingual. A later proposal sought to describe it as a Hindi-Telugu bilingual with some portions filmed in Tamil, citing interviews and a news report; opponents argued that this interpretation went beyond what the sources established.

2020.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to describe drivers as having tested positive for COVID-19, the wording commonly used in cited reports, or to name SARS-CoV-2, the virus detected by the test, to avoid implying a diagnosis of the disease. They considered alternatives such as “the coronavirus” or wording that names the virus and explains its link to COVID-19, but participants also raised concerns about confusion and precision.

2021.summary: Editors disagreed over how the opening paragraph should describe the series’ link to the Marvel comics: some objected that “featuring” could imply the comic-book version appears in the show, while others supported that wording or opposed a longer alternative as harder to read. They also questioned whether “crime thriller” and “procedural” should be listed as genres, with one editor seeking their removal and others arguing the series still had those elements or that classifying them as genres was debatable.

Editors disagreed over whether the main-cast section should follow episode credit billing or distinguish actors whose characters appeared briefly from the show's central cast. Some argued that billing should determine who is listed as main cast, while others said that listing briefly appearing actors there could mislead readers and wanted them moved to another section.

2023.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to classify the April test as a failure because it did not reach orbit, or a partial failure because it cleared the launch tower, which one editor described as the primary goal. Some proposed identifying the flight separately as a prototype test, while others argued that the usual launch-status label should apply without a special prototype distinction.

2019.summary: Editors disagreed over whether AEW wrestlers could be described as employees: one argued that the available source did not establish that status for all wrestlers, while another initially relied on language describing them as employees before accepting that the source was insufficient. The discussion also questioned a separate claim about employee status, benefits, and contract permissions, with an editor saying the cited material did not support those points.

2023.summary: Editors debated whether the article should describe Gwen Stacy as a transgender allegory: one argued that the colors do not establish that she is transgender, while another supported presenting the idea as an interpretation rather than something confirmed by the film or its creators.

2021.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the film’s infobox should list Chinese as well as English: one argued that the amount of Chinese dialogue made it a primary language, while others said the infobox should list only English as the primary language, citing template guidance and a classification site. They also disagreed about where to put streaming-viewership information, with one side favoring the home-media section and the other arguing that streaming is not home media and could belong in the reception section.

Editors disputed whether to identify the alternate Doctor Strange as Strange Supreme from the animated series: one editor objected that the source only speculated about the connection and said it was unconfirmed.

2019.summary: Editors disputed whether the Superman shown as Earth-75’s version was played by Tyler Hoechlin: some cited reports identifying him, while others argued the reports were guesses based on a trailer and wanted the identification removed until it was clarified. The entry was later removed after another source was brought into the discussion.

Editors disputed whether the article should call the show's twist “Edge of Extinction” or “Extinction Island” after a change to the former name was reverted. One editor argued for “Edge of Extinction,” pointing to the name used in episodes and on-screen, while acknowledging that an interview had used “Extinction Island.”

Editors disputed whether a Washington Post/ABC poll should count toward Tulsi Gabbard’s debate qualification, because the poll’s results were interpreted differently and the campaign challenged reports that it did not qualify. Some favored recording her count as two, others argued for three or a disputed range, with proposals to explain the disagreement in the article.

2022.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to use a detailed News18 closing tally or higher reports putting the film’s worldwide gross at ₹1,240–1,250 crore; one objection was that News18 had stopped tracking while the film was still running in some regions.

2019.summary: Editors disagreed over which election summary box to use: one argued that the standard election box could omit important party information when more than nine parties qualified, while another favored the more compact legislative-election box. They also disagreed over whether to add leaders’ photographs or party-group labels; opponents said photographs took up too much space and labels could prompt disputes over how to classify parties.

2024.summary: Editors disputed whether the opening paragraph gave too much space to criticism of Trump while saying little about Harris, with some calling for the material to be shortened or moved into the article’s main text. Others argued that prominent, well-sourced controversies about Trump belonged in the summary and that coverage should reflect the emphasis of reliable sources rather than aim for equal treatment of both candidates.

2019.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include Catalonia among potential participants: one argued its participation was speculative under current rules, while another said its broadcasters had expressed ambitions to join and that it could participate if Spain did not.

2020.summary: Editors disputed whether Hungary and Montenegro should be described as having withdrawn or simply not returning: one view reserved withdrawal for countries that had committed to participate and later pulled out, while another noted that sources commonly used the term for countries that did not participate the following year.

2019.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the infobox should call Guaidó Venezuela’s acting president, even with a visible note that the position was disputed, or avoid that title because it could present a contested claim as fact. They also differed over how prominently to explain his constitutional basis for the claim and international recognition, while some argued that the article should attribute the claim rather than call him president outright.

Editors disagreed over whether the opening paragraph gave too much weight to claims that the film had discrepancies: one objected to wording that seemed to treat those claims as established, while another argued that the account of the film’s different versions and criticism of it belonged there. They also disputed how to present the film’s reception, with one editor objecting to wording that framed the director’s comments as discrediting the film and another calling for less favorable reviews to be included.

Editors disagreed over whether Belarus’s rejection of foreign intervention and statements describing Maduro as president showed support for him; some argued they did, while others said Belarus had made no explicit statement of support. They also disputed how to describe the Organization of American States: discussion distinguished its rejection of Maduro’s inauguration from its failure to pass a resolution supporting Guaidó, while an editor challenged the claim that the organization recognized Guaidó.

2024.summary: Editors disputed whether to describe Vennells as “disgraced” in the article’s opening paragraph: supporters pointed to media use of the term, while opponents considered it an unsupported judgment about her conduct. Some editors proposed instead describing her career and Post Office role in factual terms, while others argued that the label could be used if attributed to sources rather than stated as the article’s own judgment.

2019.summary: Editors disagreed over how the voting table should represent four houseguests chosen for banishment: some treated them as out of the game who could win re-entry, while others viewed them as still competing and not equivalent to evicted contestants. They also debated whether coverage of allegations about the selections belonged under a section on audience response, and distinguished that issue from a separate controversy over another contestant’s conduct.

2020.summary: Editors disputed whether contestants who received critiques but were declared safe should be marked as having high or low placements, or simply as safe; one request proposed high and low labels, while a reply argued that safe contestants had no low placement without being in danger of elimination.

2019.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the party should be described as single-issue: some said its campaign focused on Brexit, while others argued it was intended to develop a wider platform and should not receive that label. They also contested how to describe its political outlook, particularly whether to call it populist or right-wing and whether the populism label needed attribution or explanation; others favored using the label more directly, while some urged waiting for further policy evidence before calling it right-wing.

2020.summary: Editors disagreed over how to classify the film in the opening sentence: some wanted science fiction named alongside other genres, while others argued it should use a single genre reflecting the majority of reliable sources. They also debated whether several genres made the opening sentence more informative or cluttered, with proposals ranging from naming multiple genres there to describing the film’s varied influences later in the opening section.

2023.summary: Editors disagreed over reported collections for films including Lucifer and Bheeshma Parvam, with one editor saying figures had been corrected repeatedly and another asking for reliable sources verifying them. One editor said the list should count theatrical ticket sales rather than revenue from other sources, while the other said figures that could not be verified should be removed.

2019.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to rename the article “Change UK” or use a longer title incorporating “The Independent Group,” as the party and media used different names. Some argued that “Change UK” had become the common name, while others favored the combined title or delaying a move because it was unclear which name was most widely used.

2023.summary: Editors disputed whether Rhea Ripley should be credited with one more second in the women’s Royal Rumble than Liv Morgan, who entered at the same time and was eliminated by Ripley at the finish. Some argued to use WWE’s separate recorded times, while others questioned relying on that primary source and treated the final elimination as the end of the match. One editor argued that using WWE’s timing was appropriate because other sources did not provide the same precise individual times.

2024.summary: A representative of Sinner’s management asked to remove references to former sponsors, saying the page contained false information and that the agency handled his sponsorships. An editor replied that changes required reputable independent published sources, prompting the representative to ask what evidence could establish that partnerships had ended.

2019.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the article’s account was biased toward Boeing and the U.S. government: one editor argued that it downplayed criticism of Boeing and the FAA, while others rejected the charge and disputed that the article presented Boeing’s statements as fact. They also debated whether the explanation of MCAS should be shared with related articles to keep it consistent, or written separately so each article could give the system a different level of detail and use language suited to its readers.

2020.summary: Editors disagreed over shortening the opening paragraphs, with one editor removing details about the FAA’s response, revised software, COVID-19, and airlines’ return to service because those details were covered elsewhere or not in the article body. Another editor argued the opening should retain essential narrative information rather than shift it to the infobox, and considered its four paragraphs acceptably composed despite their length.

2019.summary: Editors disagreed over how much detail to include about markings on the shooter’s weapons: some argued the lengthy annotations gave the weapons too much space, while others wanted key phrases and symbols retained or explained. They also debated whether to list the victims by name, with supporters arguing the information belonged in the article and opponents saying a list added little to understanding the event and could raise privacy concerns.
An editor requested changing Hyderabad FC’s captain to Kamaljit Singh, but the request was declined because no reliable source was provided.

Editors disputed whether the article should include claims by a former cathedral architect and the head of the Catholic League questioning whether the fire was accidental. Opponents argued that the sources were unreliable, the claims gave undue weight to unofficial speculation, and fire experts had challenged the architect’s assumptions.

Editors disagreed over how to render an Oman scorer’s name: one favored using the shorter form because sources differed on the spelling of his additional name, while another preferred the form used by the Asian Football Confederation and in earlier competitions.

2021.summary: Editors disagreed over whether Indonesia’s table entry should show only that it had advanced to an Asian Cup qualifying phase, or also mark that it could no longer advance in the World Cup qualifiers. They also disputed what to say about how runners-up would qualify for the Asian Cup: some proposed conclusions from calculations and regulations, while others argued that those outcomes were unsupported and should not be stated until confirmed by the governing body.

2020.summary: Editors disagreed over listing Germany, Saint Lucia, and Sweden as withdrawals: some said their participation had been confirmed, while others said the claim lacked reliable sourcing and should wait for confirmation.

2019.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to describe Archie as “biracial,” “multiracial” or “mixed-race,” with some objecting to the first term and others arguing it fit the cited source and referred to someone from two ethnic backgrounds. They also disputed a newspaper’s claim that he was the first “half-American, biracial royal baby”: some wanted it removed or qualified as referring to the British royal family, while another editor argued it should remain attributed to the newspaper.

2024.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the infobox should display the National Electoral Council’s announced vote count: some argued that disputed figures should be omitted, while others favored including the official results with the controversy explained. Others proposed showing both the council’s count and the opposition coalition’s tally, and editors debated whether their maps belonged near the opening or in the results section.

2023.summary: One editor requested adding Bonnie Aarons to the infobox cast list, and the change was marked done. Another exchange concerned whether the plot text had mistakenly used “Jacques” instead of “Maurice”; the editor raising it said the passage had been corrected before they could provide it as evidence.

2019.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to describe the wider movement as protests or riots: some argued that violent incidents made the latter label appropriate, while others said it would mischaracterize a movement that also included peaceful demonstrations and other nonviolent actions. They also disputed how the opening paragraph should describe violence, with some objecting that mentioning protesters’ assaults without comparable context about attacks on protesters was one-sided, while others argued that omitting protester violence distorted the account.

2020.summary: Editors disagreed over whether suicides linked to the protests should be included in the infobox death total: some supported counting them, while others said disagreement among sources made a number inappropriate. They also debated how much detail the opening paragraph should give about two deaths, with some preferring names and a total only and others arguing that the circumstances should remain because they were central to the controversy.

2019.summary: Editors disagreed over whether four songs from the album merited separate articles or should be covered in the album page; supporters of merging said the pages had little content and chart positions alone did not establish notability, while opponents cited chart impact and media coverage. They also disputed which genres belonged in the album’s genre listing: one editor argued that genres describing only individual songs should be excluded, while another pointed to country influences across several tracks.

2020.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to mention Tatiana Maslany’s denial of reports that she had been cast as She-Hulk: one argued it was relevant, while others favored emphasizing later reports confirming the casting or leaving the denial out of the phase overview. They also disagreed over whether the television series should be listed before the films because WandaVision was set to be the phase’s first release, or whether films should remain first.

2021.summary: Editors disagreed over whether reports described one Wakanda-based series featuring Okoye or two separate projects: one editor read several reports as describing a single show, while another argued the original report only confirmed an Okoye spin-off and treated a separate Wakanda series as uncertain.

2022.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to place She-Hulk according to Disney+’s timeline or after Shang-Chi: one editor argued the platform’s timeline placements had been unreliable and pointed to the director’s comments and Bruce’s injuries, while another said Disney+’s placement was acceptable given comments that the series takes place a relatively short time later.

2020.summary: Editors disagreed over whether Kemp Powers should be identified as a co-director in the film’s information box: one editor wanted his role visible there, while another said the box does not include co-director credits and noted that Powers was already mentioned in the article’s opening paragraph. They also disagreed over whether the plot summary should mention Terry telling viewers that the movie is over, with one editor proposing its inclusion and another saying it was not important to the plot.

2019.summary: Editors disputed whether to describe Ngo’s assailants as antifa or use more cautious wording, with some arguing that reliable sources identified the attackers and others pointing to sources that left their identities or affiliations uncertain. They also disagreed over whether Ngo’s account of a hammer incident and criticism of his reporting should appear in the article, and whether he should be labeled a journalist or a writer; objections focused on sourcing, wording, and the risk of implying intent.

2020.summary: Editors disputed whether the Cider Riot footage should be described as showing Patriot Prayer members planning an attack or as an alleged plan amid a brawl, and whether the disputed episode belonged in the article’s opening paragraph. They also disagreed over how to characterize Ngo, including whether to call him a journalist and whether to use the more critical label “provocateur,” with objections focusing on differing source descriptions and the weight or attribution those labels required.

Editors disagreed over whether to keep a separate section for miniseries or place those shows in genre sections and identify them by their status; one editor argued the section helped readers find limited-run shows, while another favored grouping programs by genre. They also questioned whether Doom Patrol belonged in the co-productions category because it streamed on two services, with a reply arguing that co-production meant collaboration between separate companies.

Editors disagreed over whether to divide the unusually long endorsements list into separate pages for political and non-political endorsements: supporters proposed a split because of its size. Opponents argued that non-political endorsements made up only a small part, and that splitting would not solve the length problem or match the format of most earlier campaign endorsement lists.

2019.summary: Editors debated whether the article should connect the manifesto’s language about an “invasion” to Donald Trump and conservative media, with one proposal drawing on a New York Times analysis of similarities in their language. Others questioned whether shared words were enough to establish a meaningful connection and argued that the article should explain what the claimed similarities involved.

2023.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include details about analysts’ praise, preseason performances and records, with some calling the additions too trivial and another arguing they were useful context. The discussion ended with records kept in a notes section, while interviews and opinions were removed.

2019.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the section about the controversy surrounding Donald Trump’s comments and a marked-up hurricane map belonged in the hurricane article: some called for its removal, while others argued that the coverage justified including it. They also disputed its length, with one editor proposing a single paragraph and another arguing that it could remain substantial while the story was still in the news.

2022.summary: Editors disputed whether the article adequately explained objections to the casting: one said it largely omitted the objections’ substance, including claims about Tolkien’s descriptions, while another said the article already addressed the argument that the casting conflicted with Tolkien’s intended British mythology. They also disagreed over how to frame the backlash, with one editor arguing that coverage largely opposed it and justified the section’s emphasis, while others challenged the balance and sourcing of that account.

Editors disagreed over whether to keep separate subsections for topics such as music and animation within the production section. One side said the headings would make information easier to find, while the other argued that sections with very little text would clutter the article and interrupt its flow.

2021.summary: Editors questioned whether an image should be captioned as a “teaser poster” or a “promotional image,” and the caption was changed to the latter.

2020.summary: Editors disagreed over whether English translations in parentheses should be treated as part of song titles in the contest article: one editor argued they were translations rather than titles, while another pointed to the official album’s use of “Vidkryvai (Open Up)” as evidence that the translation belonged in the title. They also disagreed about which title to follow when sources differed, with one editor noting that the single was listed without the translation and another preferring the titles used on the album and during the contest.

2025.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the film should be called a box-office bomb before its theatrical run ended: some argued it was too early to judge, while others said reliable news coverage already used the label. Later discussion continued over whether the article should use “bomb” or the milder term “disappointment,” with editors also debating how the film’s high budget should be considered alongside its box-office earnings.

2021.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the article’s seat-change figures should compare parties’ seats at the time of the election or use results from the previous election; one editor argued that the former better reflected party gains, then changed the figures back after finding guidance calling for the latter method.

2025.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include plot details after the film opened in some territories or wait until its worldwide release; one called withholding them censorship, while another said waiting was usual practice for films. Editors also disputed whether the film should be described as the series’ final entry or only as the last one featuring Tom Cruise, with arguments referring to differing interpretations of the available sources.

2024.summary: Editors disputed how many parties the article’s election summary box should show, with some favoring a compact display of the largest parties by seats and others arguing that it left out important parts of the result. Proposals ranged from showing only three parties to adding the Scottish National Party, Sinn Féin and Reform UK, or listing every party that won seats.

2019.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to title the article a coup, a political crisis, or a government resignation: supporters of “coup” pointed to the military’s role in Morales’s departure, while opponents argued for other descriptions. They also disputed whether the term was sufficiently supported by reliable sources for the title, with the move discussion noting that sources used mixed descriptions and that “coup” was controversial and value-laden.

2025.summary: Editors disagreed over how the opening paragraph should describe Fuentes: one proposed replacing a list of charged labels with a summary of his stated political positions, while others argued that this wording softened how his politics were represented. The discussion also contested which labels belonged there, including whether to use terms such as “neo-Nazi” or “white supremacist” and whether to emphasize his self-description as a Christian nationalist.

2021.summary: Editors disagreed over whether villains belong under “supporting characters”: one editor argued that the label should mean characters who help the main characters, while others said it describes a character’s narrative role, not whether they are a hero or villain.

Editors disagreed over whether The Independent’s zero-star assessment belonged in the review ratings table: some argued it was not a review of the album’s music, while others said it was a valid review and that minority ratings could be included.
