They also debated how to explain the score in the article’s text, with one proposed wording seen as implying that both Marilyn Manson’s and DaBaby’s appearances prompted it, while another editor said the reviewer identified Manson alone as the reason.

Editors disagreed over whether the article title should call the events a genocide: some argued that this presents a disputed legal label as fact and favored the more descriptive title “Repression of Uyghurs in China.” Others defended the existing title as recognizable and argued that alternatives would either be less precise or leave out abuses beyond cultural repression.

2020.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the May 12–18 tornado activity warranted an outbreak-sequence section: one argued the period was ordinary or below normal and proposed covering only May 15–17, while another agreed the section should be narrowed to May 15–17 or 16–17. The discussion also noted that no tornadoes had been confirmed on May 13 and compared the activity with a more prolific earlier sequence.

2021.summary: Editors differed over whether the constituency table should include each seat’s incumbent party: one editor argued this information was useful, while another said it would be difficult to track because alliances and candidates had changed. The opposing editor also warned that comparing past and current results could confuse readers when alliance partners exchanged constituencies.

Editors disputed whether to report the film’s worldwide gross as about 250 crore or use higher figures, with disagreement over conflicting reports and the reliability and currency of box-office sources. One editor argued that the 250-crore figure relied on an outdated report and rejected the precision of another source, while another defended the lower estimate using available domestic and overseas totals.

2026.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the infobox should list both Metro Manila and Mallorca as residences or only one main residence; one editor cited reports of a Metro Manila residence and argued that multiple residences could be included, while another favored a single entry and said it should reflect the main residence. They also discussed whether the infobox should name only Joan Bosch, identified by the official tennis tour page as the primary coach, or could list a current coaching team when multiple coaches are genuinely working together.

2021.summary: Editors disagreed over whether Paperboy Prince belonged among the Democratic primary’s “major candidates”: one editor argued Prince met the section’s stated criteria, while others opposed the placement and questioned whether the coverage warranted it. The discussion cited Prince’s inclusion in polls and coverage in outlets such as Rolling Stone and The New Yorker, while opposing editors compared that coverage with that of candidates already listed as major.

Editors disagreed over whether information about Punjab’s demographics belonged in an article about an upcoming election: one editor objected to its inclusion, while another argued that demographics matter in elections. The editor removing the information said it was irrelevant and that predicting how demographic groups would vote would be speculation; the other described it as data about Punjab, not a prediction of voting.

2020.summary: Editors disagreed over how to describe transmission in the opening paragraph: some favored emphasizing respiratory droplets from coughing, while others argued that the wording should also account for sneezing and exhalation and convey uncertainty in the sources. The agreed wording described spread during close contact and through droplets produced by coughing or sneezing, while noting that droplets may also be produced during breathing but that transmission was not considered airborne.

Editors disagreed over whether the article’s opening paragraph or information box should present the developing missile-shootdown explanation, with some favoring its inclusion and others arguing it should remain attributed as an unconfirmed possibility until stronger evidence or investigation results were available. They also debated how to describe the competing accounts: one editor objected that calling the shootdown a “claim” cast unwarranted doubt, while another defended the wording because Iranian authorities rejected the accusation and it was not yet established as verified.

Editors disagreed over whether “China virus” and “Wuhan virus” should be mentioned as alternative names: some argued that their use in sources warranted inclusion, while others said the evidence did not establish them as common names; discussion distinguished brief treatment in a naming section from using them in the opening paragraph. Editors also disagreed over whether the article should cover the possibility of a laboratory release: some argued it lacked evidence or belonged elsewhere, while others said extensive media coverage made it worth addressing as a hypothesis.

Editors disagreed over whether the 2021 contest needed a separate article or should be treated as a continuation of the canceled 2020 contest. One editor argued that most existing information could carry over, while others said important details might change and proposed preserving the 2020 article for preparations before cancellation and using the 2021 article for what followed.

2024.summary: Editors disagreed over which 20th Century Studios logo should represent the studio on the film list. One argued that the horizontal 2021 logo was still a corporate logo despite being used mainly for Hulu films, while another favored the 2020 logo, citing its wider use and presence on the studio website.

2020.summary: Editors disputed whether the song listing should name Zedd alongside Alessia Cara: one request argued for adding him, while another editor said the table should follow the credit shown during the broadcast, which named Cara alone.

Editors disagreed over whether allegations that China had deliberately underreported infections and deaths merited prominent treatment in the opening paragraph: some called for a prominent warning, while others challenged the strength and scope of the evidence behind those allegations. They also disputed how to describe the claims, with one editor objecting that vague references to news organizations could lend them undue authority and arguing that the specific people or groups making them should be identified, including their political interests where relevant.

Editors disagreed over whether Rhode Island’s stops of New Yorkers during the pandemic fit an article about xenophobia and racism: some argued that people from another U.S. state were not foreigners or a racial group, and that the stops did not amount to the kinds of serious incidents covered elsewhere. Others argued that xenophobia can target people seen as outside a community even within one nation, while also noting that the incident might not merit inclusion in the article.

Editors disputed whether a “flattening the curve” graphic accurately represented the sources: critics said it misrepresented them and should not be used, while defenders argued it illustrated two goals of intervention—spreading cases over time and reducing their total number.

Editors disagreed over whether disputed claims about public mask use should be described as misinformation: some argued that officials’ unsupported or conflicting statements qualified, while others saw the mask debate as a public discussion among experts rather than misinformation. The disagreement also included a proposal to move the mask section to a separate article, with one editor arguing that the material belonged under the misinformation topic and another finding no clear reason to split it.

2021.summary: Editors disagreed over whether an accidental laboratory escape belonged in an article about misinformation: some argued it was a legitimate possibility that should not be treated as misinformation, while others said misinformation about the scenario warranted coverage and cited scientific assessments that it was unlikely. They also disputed how to distinguish an accidental escape of a naturally occurring virus from claims that the virus was deliberately engineered or released, with critics saying that treating these as one subject could mislead readers.

2020.summary: Editors discussed how to describe the show's creator credits after later episode openings reportedly named Dan Schneider and Dana Olsen as creators and Christopher J. Nowak as developer, while earlier credits and press materials reportedly named Nowak as creator. One editor suggested following the later episodes and adding a note about the change, while another questioned how to handle the discrepancy between those credits and earlier sources.

2022.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the season’s plot summary should explain Nacho’s reason for killing himself: one argued it should describe events without inferring motives unless confirmed by the show or its creators, while another said the circumstances made his distrust of Gus clear.

2020.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include a claim that Greece ranked near the bottom of OECD countries for testing on April 30, with one side calling the figure outdated and misleading and another arguing that it was useful historical data. They also disputed whether testing information belonged in the opening paragraph or in a statistics subsection; a proposal to place it in that subsection drew support from both participants in the exchange.

Editors disagreed over whether to move England-specific material to a separate article and give more space to the distinct responses of Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland, or retain substantial England coverage because it accounted for most of the UK’s population and reported cases and deaths. They also disputed how to describe government announcements: some wanted clearer labels distinguishing UK-wide actions from England-only rules, while others argued that UK government statements could apply across the country even when implementation differed among its nations.

Editors disagreed over whether to omit the newest days from death charts because delayed registrations could make recent figures look artificially low: some favored cutting those days, while others argued for including the available figures with an explanatory note or updating them consistently. Editors also disputed whether the article’s coverage of the government response should move to a separate article; one editor argued a split would make the main article more manageable, while another favored keeping relevant material in it and trimming it instead.

Editors disagreed over which figures to use when government case counts lagged state announcements: some favored alternative sources for more timely daily case totals, while others warned that crowdsourced figures were unverified and prioritized consistent government data. One proposed approach was to use a single source for each chart or figure, while keeping government figures for cumulative totals.

Editors disagreed over whether Cy Goddard should be identified as Japanese: one argued that his Japan youth-team representation supported the label, while another said it did not establish his citizenship and asked for reliable evidence before changing the listing.

2022.summary: Editors disputed whether the film’s critical reception should be described as negative or mixed to positive: some argued that reviewers’ low ratings supported a negative label, while others called for a more favorable description and were asked to provide suitable sources. They also disagreed about which outlets to trust for box-office figures, with one editor challenging Pinkvilla’s reliability and others favoring it or Bollywood Hungama.

Editors disagreed about where to place Lance Stroll in the entries table relative to Nico Hülkenberg and Sebastian Vettel: one position put Stroll first based on the drivers entered for the opening round, while another put him after both drivers based on the season’s original lineup. The disagreement reflected competing approaches to ordering drivers—by the opening-round entries or by the original season entries and driver numbers.

2021.summary: One editor argued that the box-office section was too long and poorly organized, while another opposed removing the Japan and worldwide tables, citing gaps in other sources’ market data and the film’s Japanese box-office performance. Editors also disagreed over whether material about royalties and the author’s profits belonged in an “Issues” section: one characterized it as ordinary industry practice, while another argued that the reported pay concerns were controversies worth including.

2020.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the tornado table should include only events explicitly confirmed by weather authorities or also unconfirmed reports; some argued reports could be included while awaiting surveys, while others insisted on documented confirmation. They also questioned how to count deaths when the overall toll did not match the tornado-by-tornado totals, and whether deaths not confirmed as tornado-related belonged in the outbreak’s figures.

Editors disagreed over whether to include victims’ names and personal details in the article: some argued that coverage in reliable sources warranted including them, while others preferred linking to an external victim list instead. Some editors favored naming victims only when they had been specifically targeted or were otherwise notable; others argued that information about victims should be represented when prominent in sources.

2022.summary: Editors disagreed over whether candidates’ policy positions should appear in a comparison table or be written as prose; supporters said a table would make comparison easier and reduce subjective selection, while opponents said it would impose questionable categories and could imply candidates lacked policies where none were listed. Some editors favored putting the information into candidate biographies instead, arguing that prose would preserve context about what a party leader could actually do.

2020.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include reports that Indian soldiers had been held and released: some wanted the reports removed after official denials, while others argued that reporting by news outlets merited mention with the denials attributed. They also disputed how to describe reports of 35 Chinese losses, with one editor favoring “casualties” because the figure might include both deaths and serious injuries, and others favoring the source’s wording of “killed.”

Editors disagreed over whether “Never Really Over” and “Harleys in Hawaii,” released before the album was announced but later added to its track list, should be classified as singles from Smile. One view treated them as standalone releases before the album’s promotional campaign, with “Daisies” identified as the lead single; another argued their later inclusion and use in album promotion made them Smile singles.

Editors differed over whether the television information box should show the planned four-episode total before any episodes aired; one editor supported listing the known total, while others said the count should be added as episodes were released.

2021.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to describe the release primarily as a four-part miniseries or a single four-hour movie: one argued that the planned miniseries format remained in place, while another cited reports presenting it as a movie and said there was no proof the filmmaker’s statement was untrue. They also disputed how to characterize critical reception, with one editor arguing that sources showed mixed feedback and another preferring to avoid an overall label because sources differed.

2022.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the opening paragraph should describe the film as having received “critical acclaim” or use the more qualified phrase “generally positive”; one editor argued the stronger wording relied too heavily on an aggregator’s label, while another disputed that characterization and the proposed replacement.

2020.summary: Editors disagreed over whether NiziU’s music should be described as K-pop, J-pop or a hybrid: one argued that its Korean production and training supported a K-pop framing, while another pointed to the group’s Japanese origin and Apple Music categorization in favor of J-pop.

2021.summary: Editors disagreed over whether ATK Mohun Bagan should be described as a new merged club or as the continuation of Mohun Bagan, with some pointing to its use of Mohun Bagan’s registration and others emphasizing evidence that the clubs had merged. They also disputed which sources should guide that account: some treated the club’s official website and registration as decisive, while others argued that the article should rely on independent reporting.

2020.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include West’s bipolar disorder in the campaign article: one argued that it gave context to his conduct, while another questioned whether sources connected the condition to the campaign and whether including it was appropriate. They also disputed a sentence asserting that violence in Chicago predated the welfare state, with an editor arguing that the cited article described earlier causes of violence rather than establishing that claim.

2025.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include the online allegations that Piker used a shock collar on his dog: supporters pointed to coverage of the dispute, including a report on animal-rights group PETA’s response, and argued for a brief, neutral account. Opponents said the reporting was largely based on gossip or unsubstantiated claims and did not establish lasting importance, so the allegations should be left out.

2021.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to list Dutch and English as languages for the Dutch entry before its song was selected: one argued that the languages were certain, while others said the listing could be misleading until the entry was confirmed. They also disputed whether an Armenian news report was reliable enough to confirm Maléna Fox’s participation, with editors questioning its sourcing and others saying an unaffiliated source could still be usable if reliable.

2025.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include Mamdani’s interview response to a question about “globalize the intifada” in his biography: some argued the coverage and public debate warranted a brief mention, while others considered it an isolated campaign issue that did not belong in a biography. They also disputed how to describe his response, with some favoring wording that he declined to condemn the phrase and others arguing that this implied support or misrepresented what he said.

2023.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the page should use UEFA’s association names, such as “Czechia,” or retain country names used elsewhere on Wikipedia; one editor favored matching UEFA, while another said established Wikipedia naming choices should govern, including distinguishing the Republic of Ireland from the island of Ireland.

2021.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the opening paragraph should say the Act restricts devolved governments’ powers in practice, as several academic analyses were said to conclude, or focus on its mutual-recognition and non-discrimination rules without presenting that interpretation as fact. Some argued those analyses addressed an earlier version of the bill and that amendments changed its effects; others maintained the amendments did not substantially alter the provisions affecting devolution.

2020.summary: Editors disputed whether the article should give a combined death toll in its infobox: one proposed combining deaths discussed in separate reports, while another objected that this would create a total neither source reported and instead used a source’s own figure. They also questioned whether deaths with varied circumstances could be classified together without a reliable source explicitly making that connection.

2021.summary: Editors disagreed over how much information about countries not participating should appear in the article: one favored limiting the section to information directly about the 2022 contest, while others argued that explanations for countries shown on the map and annual participation decisions belonged there. The proposal to keep the section shorter was met with agreement that the page should explain the map, and the initial editor accepted the other arguments.

2025.summary: Editors disagreed over how to open the article: some proposed leading with the season’s three Category 5 hurricanes and Hurricane Melissa, while another suggested describing its pattern of active and quiet stretches. Others argued the first sentence should define what an Atlantic hurricane season is before highlighting distinctions, and objected to emphasizing Melissa or technical measures in the opening.

2020.summary: Editors disagreed over whether Syrian fighters recruited for Azerbaijan should appear as combatants and how their role should be described. Some argued reporting supported including them, while others questioned whether fighters recruited individually represented the Syrian National Army, and debated how to reflect denials by Azerbaijan and Turkey.

Editors disagreed over which satellite image should appear at the top of the article: some favored an image from Delta’s strongest winds, while others preferred a later image showing a clearer eye and lower pressure. Those favoring the strongest-winds image said the later one showed a weaker storm; supporters of the later image argued that it gave a more representative view of Delta’s appearance.

2022.summary: Editors disputed whether the article should describe the declaration’s “focused protection” approach as fringe: one side sought to remove or qualify the label, while others argued it should remain because they considered it supported by reliable sources. The discussion also rejected using the authors’ credentials alone to settle how the approach should be characterized.

2021.summary: Editors disputed whether to include South Atlantic system 01Q in the year’s cyclone list, since NOAA tracked it but the Brazilian Navy did not recognize it. They also disagreed over whether it was tropical or subtropical, and whether the available records supported calling it a storm rather than a weaker system.

2024.summary: Editors disagreed over whether Dean Phillips belonged in the results box: some argued that being the second-place human candidate or receiving delegates justified inclusion, while others said existing criteria did not allow it or that Jason Palmer’s contest win took priority. They also disputed whether New Hampshire’s January primary vote should count in the overall totals, with some supporting its inclusion as a real vote and others objecting that it was not approved by the Democratic National Committee.

2021.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the opening paragraph should describe Şahin as Turkish as well as German, or mention that he was born in Turkey. One position emphasized his German citizenship and argued that ethnicity or birthplace did not belong in the opening unless relevant to his notability; the other cited his self-identification and media coverage to argue that his Turkish background was relevant.

2026.summary: Editors disputed whether the campaign-background section gave too much weight to arguments that Haley Stevens was more electable and to criticism of Abdul El-Sayed. Some argued that the presentation was slanted and called for balancing information, including polling, while others defended it as a sourced account of supporters’ arguments and opposed using polling to declare one candidate more electable.

Editors disagreed over whether the article’s opening paragraphs should name minor-party nominees and a write-in candidate, or focus on candidates considered consequential to the race. One editor argued that winning a party nomination or having a reported write-in campaign justified mention, while another said candidates needed to make an impact on the election, including through polling, to merit inclusion.

Editors disagreed over when statements of support that do not use the word “endorse” should qualify for the article’s endorsement list; one editor argued that unequivocal public support can count, while another questioned whether a donor’s support belonged there rather than in campaign-finance coverage. They also disagreed over whether hosting a fundraiser counts as an endorsement, with one editor saying it does and another saying it does not.

2020.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the article should have a separate section listing Hurricane Iota’s records: some argued the records deserved their own section, while another editor called such a section trivia and preferred placing records in the storm’s history. They also disputed what should qualify, with one editor proposing that a separate section wait until it could include about five meaningful records not already covered elsewhere, while others cited records they considered important.

2021.summary: Editors disputed whether the book’s treatment of rapid-onset gender dysphoria should be called “fringe,” or instead described as a contentious idea that is not recognized as a medical diagnosis. Those arguing for “fringe” pointed to professional organizations’ rejection of the concept and the lack of supporting clinical evidence, while opponents said medical sources described it as proposed and in need of further study, not conclusively disproven.
Editors disagreed over whether “penguinz0” should be treated as one of MoistCr1tikal’s aliases: one argued that it was not, while another said it was.

2023.summary: Editors disagreed over which of two satellite images of Hurricane Beatriz should appear in the article: one editor favored the first image, while several others preferred the second, describing it as clearer and more representative of the storm.

2022.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the opening paragraph should say the film presents the exodus as a genocide, or treat that description as the filmmakers’ claim rather than an established fact; one editor argued it reflects the film’s portrayal, while another said it did not belong in the opening paragraph. They also disputed whether to say the film promotes anti-Muslim prejudice or to frame this only as an accusation made by critics, with editors pointing to reviews that used different degrees of criticism.

2021.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include the July 2021 Baghdad bombing: one said it did not meet the article’s inclusion criteria, while another argued the event was large enough to be memorable.

Editors disagreed over whether a candidate’s campaign website was enough to support listing individual endorsements: one side considered campaigns reliable sources about their own endorsements, while the other argued that independent reporting was needed, particularly for endorsers not named in news coverage.

Editors disputed the event’s name: some argued “attack” was more common in reliable coverage, while others preferred “riot” or “storming,” which they considered more precise or neutral descriptions. They also disagreed over whether the article should call the event an “insurrection” in its own voice, with some pointing to reliable sources using that term and others objecting that it could imply unproven criminal intent.

Editors disagreed over whether the article should have a separate section on the Wuhan laboratory leak possibility: one position was that it gave undue prominence to a fringe idea and repeated material covered elsewhere. Others argued that investigations into a possible laboratory accident warranted their own subsection, while distinguishing that scientific inquiry from conspiracy claims about deliberate release or bioweapons.

Editors disagreed over whether to list interim manager Graeme Jones: one argued that earlier season tables left out temporary managers when a permanent replacement arrived, while others favored including any interim manager who took charge of a game. They also questioned whether Ole Gunnar Solskjær’s departure should be labeled a sacking or a departure by mutual consent, pointing to differing descriptions and unclear club statements.

2026.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the opening paragraph should foreground the accusations of academic misconduct, which some saw as central to Arday’s public profile, or give more space to his career and the circumstances following his resignation and death. They also debated whether that paragraph should mention criticism of the media scrutiny, with some arguing that it should include both criticism and defenses of the reporting, while others favored leaving the media debate to later paragraphs or omitting it there.

2025.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to move Tropical Depression Wilma into the season article’s section for other systems, with one editor saying it should move unless significant damage or deaths were reported, while another urged waiting for damage updates. The case for keeping a fuller account cited the storm’s length, wind warnings, and preparations in the Philippines; another editor said the section should be shortened and questioned whether the depression merited more coverage.

2026.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the list should cover only professional football or include Robert Carmona, whom one editor described as a professional because he played with the squad throughout the season and who was said to hold a Guinness World Record.

2021.summary: Editors disagreed over how to arrange newly stolen performers in the teams table: one wanted them kept in their original positions, while another said they should be placed alphabetically, with battle losers at the end of the row.

2023.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the opening summary should mention the 2023 U.S. Department of Energy assessment favoring a laboratory origin with low confidence, alongside the FBI’s view. Some argued these assessments deserved more prominence, while others said the development reflected one agency changing its view among eight and was not important enough for an already lengthy opening summary.

2022.summary: Editors disagreed over whether The Owl House’s shortened final season should be described as a planned ending or as a cancellation, with some attributing it to Disney’s view of the show’s brand and others rejecting that account and pointing to the creator’s intention for the season to be final. A separate disagreement concerned how many of actor Billy Kametz’s animation voice roles to include in the page’s death entry: one editor proposed a longer list, while another objected to the requested additions.

Editors disagreed over whether to list Manya Singh as eliminated: one objected that the claim lacked a reliable source, noting she had appeared in an episode, while another had repeatedly added the elimination.

2025.summary: Editors disputed whether Square Enix’s description of Forspoken’s sales as “lacklustre” belonged in the article’s opening paragraph: supporters considered the publisher’s comments useful context where actual sales figures were unavailable, while opponents argued that the remark reflected an internal target and deserved less prominence. The discussion focused on placing that specific sales comment in the opening paragraph, rather than on labeling the game a commercial failure.

2021.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to keep the contestant progress table: some considered it a useful summary, while others argued it duplicated information and included rankings that were not supported by sources. They also disputed whether the table should show contestants as having high or low placements, with supporters saying those labels capture important nuance and opponents viewing them as interpretations that should not be presented without reliable sourcing.

2023.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the opening paragraph should call the film a sequel, a prequel, or standalone, with objections that these labels could confuse readers and a counterargument that the film was confirmed as a prequel. They also disputed whether to describe its relationship to the earlier films as a reboot or as part of their continuity, with editors interpreting comments by the director and other sources differently.

2025.summary: Editors disagreed over how to describe Sławomir Mentzen’s position before the runoff: one argued that he made no endorsement and told supporters to choose for themselves, while another said his statement ruling out a vote for Rafał Trzaskowski supported describing him as opposed to Trzaskowski. The discussion also noted his favorable remarks about Karol Nawrocki, while differing over what those remarks implied.

2024.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the article’s election-issues section presented campaign claims and voter-behavior speculation as established issues, and whether its sources supported those claims; the section’s defender said sources substantiated the material and was open to rewording it. They also disputed whether to list the new party JLKM among the main contestants before the election: one editor pointed to the number of seats it planned to contest, while another argued that contesting many seats was not enough and that it should first win seats.

2022.summary: Editors questioned whether a reported Pongal 2023 release date could be included in the infobox without an official announcement, with one noting that publication of release information elsewhere changed the immediate issue but not the broader concern about Wikipedia reporting ahead of confirmation.

2023.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include an independent analysis of the election results, including reasons attributed to the BRS defeat, or keep the article focused on government formation. One editor pointed to the article layout’s guidance on aftermath, while another supported restoring the analysis with additional sources and neutral wording, citing a previous election article as an example.

2026.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the plot summary should put events in chronological order or follow the film’s order of revelations. One argued that jumping between past and present makes the summary harder to follow and noted that the book’s article uses chronological order; another said the film’s flashbacks gradually reveal information that affects how viewers interpret the story.

2022.summary: Editors disagreed about where to place the Bahamas and South Korea in the article’s alphabetical country list: one position favored listing them under B and K using inverted names, while another argued that South Korea should remain under S and that the Bahamas belongs under B.

2021.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include a note about Rose and Giovanni’s Week 8 performance and the judges’ comments: one argued the detail about Rose’s deafness merited mention, while another said this section generally records only missed performances or withdrawals and does not include judges’ remarks.

2022.summary: Editors disputed whether the article should say Malone promoted misinformation or instead attribute that characterization to critics, with some arguing that the wording overstated what was established and others pointing to reliable-source coverage of the criticism. They also disagreed over how to describe his role in mRNA vaccine technology: one proposal said his patent supported calling him an inventor, while another editor argued he was not the inventor and that wording such as “claimed” was appropriate.

2024.summary: Editors disagreed over whether summaries of Cody Rhodes’s storyline went beyond what cited reports supported, including wording about his choice of opponent and what he would eventually pursue. They also disputed whether to explain how Rhodes’s decision related to Roman Reigns, with one editor arguing the storyline could be described without Reigns and the other saying his role was necessary to explain how the match came about.

2025.summary: Editors disputed which parties several candidates elected on the PD–ASHM coalition’s list belonged to: one list placed Erisa Xhixho under PD, while a correction assigned her and several others to PL and said the remaining candidates belonged to PD.

2024.summary: Editors disputed whether to include RealClearPolitics in the polling table: some argued its averages were less reliable because it did not filter out low-quality polls or weight results, while others noted that other aggregators also included right-leaning pollsters and argued for including it.

2023.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the plot summary should specifically mention Barbie being groped and punching the man: one argued that the incident could be covered by a broader description of events, while another said it was an assault and an important turning point in the story.

2024.summary: Editors disagreed over which actors to identify as the series’ main cast: one approach used the actors appearing in episode opening credits, while another suggested using the actors named in Disney’s pre-release material. They also questioned how to describe the series’ connection to the Marvel Cinematic Universe, with one editor citing its Disney+ placement and another noting that it was not on the service’s timeline and questioning whether that placement was correct.

2026.summary: Editors disagreed over how to show Bangladesh’s place in the tournament: one argued it should remain listed until an official withdrawal or expulsion, while others discussed showing it as withdrawn or replaced by Scotland, with differing views on whether to strike it out or explain the change in a note. They also disputed how to present prize money, after an editor said the table mixed teams’ total awards with amounts for reaching a stage and reverted it to a different presentation.

2022.summary: An edit request sought to rank Vikram first as the year’s highest-grossing Tamil film, but the response said the cited article described it as close to ₹250 crore and only set to become the year’s highest-grossing film.

Editors disagreed over whether to call the gatherings before Prince Philip’s funeral “parties”: some cited multiple news reports using that term, while others preferred the more neutral “gatherings” because the events’ character was disputed and Sue Gray’s report used that wording.

2023.summary: Editors disputed how to describe the film’s language: one commenter questioned whether the director’s remarks meant scenes were shot only in Telugu, while another cited reporting that it was filmed simultaneously in Telugu and Hindi and restored that description.

2024.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to describe the film as bilingual or primarily Telugu, including whether limited Hindi reshoots justified mentioning Hindi in the opening paragraph. Some argued the film should be described as Telugu because its main filming was in that language, while others called it bilingual. They also disputed which worldwide box-office figures to report: some sought higher totals announced by the makers or cited by media outlets, while others questioned those figures and argued for estimates grounded in independent reporting.

2023.summary: Editors disagreed over whether Logan Sargeant should be described as an American or as a driver from the United States. One editor argued that “American” should include people across the Americas and preferred a United States-specific description, while others said English commonly uses “American” for people from the United States.

2026.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the article should say Keiko Fujimori had been elected president before Peru’s electoral commission declared a winner: one objected that she had not claimed victory and her opponent had not conceded, while another cited major news outlets that described her as having won.

Editors disputed whether reporting about a lawsuit made public on the film’s opening day belonged in the article: some connected its timing and coverage to the film’s release, while others argued the allegations predated the release and were not pertinent to the film. They also disagreed about including director Antoine Fuqua’s comments questioning accusers’ motives and a response from the director of another film about Jackson; some supported including both, while others considered Fuqua’s remarks unrelated to the film’s production and not significant enough to include.

2023.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the reported ₹222 crore box-office figure was reliable and represented gross or net takings; one argued it relied on a source considered unreliable and was a net figure, while another maintained that reputable publications’ reports supported including it.

Editors disagreed over whether to identify Rockstar North or Rockstar Studios as the game’s developer: one proposed Rockstar Studios as a stand-in while suggesting North was the main developer, while others objected that the claim was speculative and should not be included without a reliable source.

2022.summary: Editors disputed how the opening paragraph should describe Putin’s claim that Ukraine was dominated by neo-Nazis, with one editor arguing that calling it false was judgmental and should be attributed rather than stated directly. Others argued that reliable sources consistently described the claim as false, so the article should say so rather than imply an unsupported equivalence.

Editors disagreed over whether to include claims that Ukrainian forces used civilians as human shields alongside reporting on Russian forces’ use of civilians; one objected that the supporting accounts were unreliable, while another argued that reports from foreign nationals should be included.

2023.summary: Editors disputed the film’s box-office total: one request said it had never crossed 500 crore, while a reply noted that sources disagreed.

Editors disagreed over whether R-Truth should be listed as a member of The Judgment Day after a match involving him and JD McDonagh. One editor argued the match meant Truth had joined and McDonagh had left, while others said Truth was not an official member and remained outside the group.

2022.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to name the student who filmed the video and identify him as the son of journalist James Delingpole: some argued that news coverage supported including the details, while others cited privacy concerns and questioned their relevance and sourcing. They also disagreed over whether to add later outcomes from the Partygate investigations as context, with one editor saying this would help readers understand what became of the initial allegations and another arguing that it would distort what was known when Starmer made his comments.

2026.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include a Maithili name alongside Shah’s name in the article, with one editor arguing that sources identify Maithili as his mother tongue and another questioning whether the cited sources establish that he speaks it natively. They also disputed whether the sources were reliable and whether Maithili should appear alongside Nepali, including whether shared writing script or official-language status should affect its inclusion.

2022.summary: Editors disagreed over whether criticism of the police response belonged in the opening paragraph: some supported including it, while others considered it premature and said the brief summary should focus on the shooting. They also debated whether to include detailed biographies of victims; supporters said personal details could add context, while opponents considered such material irrelevant or intrusive in an article about the event.

2024.summary: One editor proposed moving the lengthy production section into a separate article, calling the film important, while other editors questioned whether it merited its own article and said published, independent, reliable sources were needed. Other editors also objected that the section was too long, disorganized, and included overly detailed material, and favored keeping it concise.

2022.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the reception summary should identify the film’s supporters and critics by political affiliation: one editor objected that the wording singled out conservative reviewers, while another favored political labels for both groups. They also disputed describing criticism as coming from multiple medical experts, with one editor saying the article cited only one person and another arguing that person’s expertise mattered more than whether he called himself an advocate.

2023.summary: Editors questioned how the article should describe the group’s political position, especially whether it should use only “far-right” or also “right-wing,” with one participant saying sources supported either label and another asking why “right-wing” had been removed. Some participants argued that labels such as “far-right” were not objective or did not fit the group, while another said they had not found Argentine sources using that description and only found it in American media.

2022.summary: Editors disputed whether Rubina and Faisal should be listed as joint runners-up or ranked first and second, respectively: one request argued that no order had been announced, while another said Rubina’s higher judges’ scores placed her ahead of Faisal.

2024.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the article should mention that the United States and China tied for the most gold medals, with one objecting that China’s performance did not belong in a U.S.-focused article and another arguing the tie was relevant context about the U.S. team. They also disputed whether silver medals should be described as a “tiebreaker”: some editors favored that wording, while others preferred saying the United States placed first overall after winning more silver medals.

2022.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the critical-reception section should say that Midnights was less innovative or substantial than Folklore and Evermore, with one editor proposing that characterization based on several reviews. Others argued those reviews did not establish a shared critical view and that including selected criticisms would overstate their prominence, while another editor supported giving the critiques limited space.

2025.summary: Editors disagreed over whether Lando Norris’s 2026 car number should be listed as undecided: one proposed “to be confirmed” because he might choose number 1, while another argued it should remain 4 unless he actually elects to change it.

2023.summary: Editors disagreed over how to present the non-championship Macau event: one proposed a separate table showing its qualifying and main race dates, while another favored keeping it in the existing calendar table with a note to distinguish the race formats.

2022.summary: Editors disagreed over how to describe the announcement of the Queen’s death: one argued that Twitter was the first public announcement and should come first in the timeline, while another said the article should also account for notices at Buckingham Palace and on the royal family website. They disputed whether the sources established the exact order of announcements and whether highlighting Twitter implied that it was the main way the news was made public.

2023.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include a reported $200 million budget for the film: one questioned the figure and called its source wrong, while another defended it as backed by a reliable source.

2024.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the article should be renamed “Wish (2023 film)” because another film had also been known as “Wish.” Some argued that “Wish” was little used as a title and the existing disambiguation page was adequate, while another pointed to headlines using “Wish” for the other film.

2022.summary: Editors disagreed over whether New Zealand should have its own section or be grouped with other Commonwealth realms; supporters cited its longstanding status as a realm and the size of its delegation, while another editor argued that countries’ size and length of independence should not determine separate treatment. Others favored grouping New Zealand with the other realms, while retaining appropriate subsections for individual countries.

2024.summary: Editors described Viking Motorsports as collaborating with RSS during the season, with the entry credited to RSS, and one editor argued it should remain listed as an RSS entry with a note about the collaboration. Another editor disputed that classification, asserting that the entry was fielded by Viking Motorsports.

2025.summary: Editors disagreed about how many guest actors to include in the series’ cast list, especially whether it should name performers with brief or one-off appearances. Some argued the list should focus on main or recurring characters and leave one-off guests to episode pages; others supported including selected guest actors based on their credits, appearances in multiple episodes, or narrative impact, while disputing which performers met that threshold.

Editors disagreed over which of Ethel Caterham’s milestones belonged in the infobox’s “known for” section, including whether to list her as the last person born in the 1900s and the last British subject of Edward VII. One editor favored including all milestones or only her status as the oldest living person, while others considered some milestones too minor and favored highlighting her as the oldest living person and oldest British person.

2023.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to list Representative Dean Phillips as retiring while he campaigned for president: one view said his presidential run meant he should be listed as retiring, while another argued that he had not announced a House retirement and pointed to earlier presidential candidates who were not listed that way.

2024.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to add Louisiana’s newly enacted congressional map immediately: one argued that legal proceedings and possible court rejection made an update premature, while another said it should be reflected because it was then the law in effect.

2026.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include the Libertarian candidate in the election infobox: one view was that the available polls did not establish the required support, while another argued that local polling put him above the threshold. The disagreement also concerned whether polls listing a candidate only as “other” could count, and whether local rather than statewide polling was relevant.

2022.summary: Editors disagreed over whether Matt Taibbi’s statement that he had seen no evidence of government involvement meant the files offered no evidence of U.S. pressure on Twitter, or referred instead to foreign-government involvement in hacking or fabricating the laptop material. They also disputed the opening paragraph’s characterization of the files as contradicting conspiracy theories: one editor argued it should say the files offered no direct support, while another maintained that the claim about FBI pressure was contradicted by the reporting.

2023.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the German entrant’s name should appear as Fia or FIA: one position favored the more common lowercase styling, while another argued for the contest organizers’ all-capital version. They also debated whether to mention brief French, English, and Spanish phrases in the German song, with some editors favoring their inclusion because they appear in the official lyrics and others questioning their audibility or significance.

Editors disagreed over how the film’s music credits should appear: one editor said Nobin Paul handled the original soundtrack and William Francis contributed only one song, and asked for their roles to be distinguished. Another editor argued that both should remain credited in the music section, citing sources that they said credited both composers.

2024.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to note Ferrari’s use of the name Scuderia Ferrari HP: one position was that the note explained its public branding, while others argued the name was absent from the official entry list and the sponsorship detail was not significant enough to include.

Editors disagreed over whether the 2025 competition should be described as the first edition of a new tournament or as an expanded version of the existing FIFA Club World Cup. They also disputed whether Inter Miami should appear in a separate invited-teams table or remain among the qualified teams, with one editor arguing that the club was invited by FIFA and another saying it qualified through the host-country place.

Editors disagreed over whether projects such as Merry Little Batman and Superman & Lois belonged in the Elseworlds section: one editor argued the label applied only after the DCU began and questioned whether the projects had been officially branded that way. Other editors said reliable sources placed the projects under Elseworlds branding and argued they should remain listed unless newer sources showed otherwise.

2023.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the April 19, 2023 tornado event warranted its own article: one argued that two deaths and 10 tornadoes fell short of the usual standard, while others favored an article based on the event’s developing scale and coverage. The discussion also raised whether a draft should remain under discussion before being moved into the main article space, though one editor said that the event’s later-confirmed tornado count made an article more reasonable.

2024.summary: The discussion centers on requests to update the candidate list, including proposed changes to candidate counts; the requests shown were not accompanied by sufficiently specific instructions or a source.

2023.summary: Editors discussed whether to add a section about controversies involving Pakistan’s national organization and allegations of sexual harassment in Indonesia to the article’s background. They also disagreed over whether to list South Sudan as a participant based on its representative’s social-media post, with one editor urging a wait for official confirmation.

2024.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include two circuit-location maps: one argued that a single world map was sufficient, while others defended the newer maps as a better way to label circuits and favored keeping the established single-map style.

2023.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the article should describe the police officers’ actions as an assault or use more specific descriptions such as beating, tasing and pepper-spraying, with some arguing that assault was legally charged and others saying the word understated what happened. They also disputed the opening paragraph’s framing of Nichols’s death: one editor objected to saying he was killed on the day of the traffic stop because he died three days later, while another argued the article must state that officers killed him.

Editors disputed which sources and figures to use for the film’s box-office totals: some proposed numbers announced by the production company or reported through Comscore, while others objected to relying on the production company and questioned figures linked to sources they considered unreliable. They also disagreed over whether reviews should be described as mixed or as mixed to positive, with one editor arguing that the presence of negative reviews supported the mixed label.

2026.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to describe the Backrooms as a “parallel universe” or as “extradimensional space.” One argued that the first term fits the film’s separate world, while another preferred the second, saying the usual fictional associations of parallel universes do not fit the Backrooms and pointing to publications that use “extradimensional.”

2023.summary: Editors disputed whether Croatia belonged in a section about countries with information specific to the 2024 contest, with one objecting that the source did not explicitly mention 2024 and another initially treating a multi-year arrangement as relevant before reconsidering. They also disagreed over whether Russia and Belarus should be mentioned, with one editor arguing they should be included alongside other countries and another saying the article lacked statements specifically about the 2024 contest.

2024.summary: Editors disagreed over how much detail the article should give to its controversies: some argued for trimming the section, while others objected that removing material would leave coverage one-sided or incomplete. They also debated whether to mention Israel’s participation controversy in the opening paragraph, with opponents calling it misplaced and supporters arguing it was prominent enough to summarize there.

Editors disagreed over whether Montenegro’s broadcaster publishing rules for a national selection was enough to list the country as intending to participate: one view said it was not an official announcement, while another treated the document as confirmation of the broadcaster’s intent.

2023.summary: Editors disagreed over whether match sources should use full citations instead of bare URLs: one argued that citation standards apply even if other football articles do not follow them, while others objected that the change departed from established practice for comparable matches.

Editors disagreed over whether preliminary damage-assessment data could be used to assign tornado ratings before the National Weather Service issued a clear statement. Some argued that frequently updated survey data could support ratings, while others said it could contain errors and wanted to wait for official statements; one editor urged keeping ratings marked as unknown until then.

2024.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the film Roohi should be treated as part of the same supernatural film universe as Stree 2; one view pointed to its omission from the Stree 2 trailer’s featured logos as evidence it was excluded. Another editor argued that the trailer did not establish Roohi’s exclusion and that earlier producer statements supported keeping it included unless the producers clearly said otherwise.

2025.summary: Editors disputed whether the season article should include an accumulated cyclone energy total calculated from data by Colorado State University, with one editor objecting that the underlying sources were not official regional agencies and did not provide a season total for this basin. They also discussed whether tropical lows belonged in the “Other Systems” section: one editor questioned their placement because the Bureau of Meteorology had covered many of them, while others supported moving back systems that could be sourced and described.

2023.summary: Editors disagreed over how to describe Healy’s discussion of watching violent pornography on a podcast: some argued he was retelling an incident rather than joking and wanted the account to reflect that, while another editor said a secondary source described the exchange as a joke. They also disputed how much detail and context to include, with one editor arguing that the wording minimized the incident and another favoring a concise, neutral account that reflected the later clarification by a host.

2025.summary: Editors disagreed over whether Vince warranted its own article: one argued it should have one like Bheki, while another said a storm’s impact on people mattered more and prioritized an article about Garance.

2024.summary: Editors disagreed over adding the finale songs before the episode aired: a request supplied song details and links to a fan wiki and an entertainment site, while a reply said the sourcing was not reliable enough and recommended waiting for the broadcast.

2025.summary: Editors disputed how to describe Zohran Mamdani’s political platform, with some favoring “democratic socialist” based on his self-description and cited coverage, while another argued that his policies were social democratic but acknowledged that this wording lacked sources. They also disagreed over whether to label him “far-left”: one editor proposed the term, while others said the cited coverage did not describe him that way and that his position could be characterized in several ways.

Editors disputed when the article should say Sri Lanka was eliminated: one argued it could still qualify after losing its first two Super Four matches, while a later reply said it was eliminated only after the India-Bangladesh match.

Editors disputed whether the Homeland Party should be described as far-right, with one view arguing that the label misrepresents the party by relying on individual members’ actions rather than its platform, and another pointing to sources that characterize the party that way. They also disagreed over whether contentious descriptions and allegations should appear in the article’s own voice or be explicitly attributed to sources, with concerns raised about sourcing and claims involving named people.

2023.summary: Editors questioned whether saying Merzouk had no criminal record was confusing when the same section described arrests and other contact with police. Some argued that the phrase meant he had no convictions, while others said the article should explain that distinction so readers would not mistake it for a claim that he had never faced accusations or arrests.

2024.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the infobox should list works that inspired the series: one argued the listed influences did not merit inclusion, while another wanted creator-identified inspirations included for accuracy. They also disagreed over whether a creator’s statements were enough, or whether an influence had to be explicitly credited within the show itself, to qualify for the infobox’s “Inspired by” field.

Editors disputed whether the opening section should describe planned replacement workers as “Trump loyalists” or as loyal to the next Republican president; some argued the former wording reflected current news coverage, while others said the project’s wording was not specific to Trump. Another editor objected that “loyalists” suggests personal allegiance and preferred a more neutral description of personnel who share an administration’s goals.

2025.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the film’s reception should be described as negative: a request sought that change and said the film was panned, while the response noted that the cited review appeared mixed.

Editors disagreed over whether the article made unconfirmed details seem nearly certain: one editor called for clearer labeling of speculation, while another said the article already identified unconfirmed details as industry rumors. They also disputed wording about users being banned for playing older Switch games on the new console; one editor said the wording lacked context and could wrongly suggest ordinary use caused bans, and asked for the circumstances described in the source to be made clear.

2023.summary: One editor sought tighter editing restrictions, saying repeated changes to the weekly summary, nominations table and status chart were disrupting the page’s format.

2024.summary: Editors disputed whether Jim Price should be listed as deceased: one editor considered forum and social-media reports sufficient, while others questioned their reliability and whether an online listing referred to the same person.

2023.summary: Editors disputed whether the opening paragraph should say that United Nations independent experts and human rights groups accused both Hamas and Israel of war crimes, or use more general wording. Supporters said naming the accused parties made the summary clearer, while critics argued it could imply equivalence between the allegations or overstate the United Nations’ position.

2024.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the article title should name Hamas or Gaza, with arguments for each name drawing on how the conflict was described and who was involved. They also disputed how casualty figures should appear in the opening paragraph: some opposed continuing to use women-and-children breakdowns after the United Nations revised its figures, while others favored reporting the overall death toll and related breakdowns with clarification. coverage_note

Editors disagreed over whether Bash in Berlin belongs in The Great American Bash chronology: one said it does, while another questioned the connection, arguing that the events share only the word “Bash” in their names.

Editors disagreed over whether the article should credit the artists as ¥$ or name Kanye West and Ty Dolla Sign separately. Supporters of ¥$ pointed to the duo name used for releases, while others favored the individual names, noting that the article’s cited coverage generally used them and arguing that article naming should follow those sources.

2025.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include George Lopez, Ice Spice, Arturo Castro and Sherry Cola in the film’s listed cast, with one side arguing that their grouped appearance in the credits qualified and another saying they should be excluded because they did not have individual billing screens. The exchange also turned on what counts as single-screen billing: one editor interpreted it to include the grouped credit screen before the full end credits, while another said it meant a screen showing one actor alone.

2024.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include only officially announced candidates or also report seat-sharing arrangements based on published sources and party leaders’ comments.

2025.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the opening should state that Israel is committing genocide as fact or attribute that characterization to organizations and scholars; some argued the genocide label remained disputed, while others said scholarly consensus supported direct wording. They also differed over how prominently the opening should present dissenting views, with some favoring a mention near the opening and others arguing that would give a minority view too much weight.

2024.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the article should remain in the encyclopedia before the film’s release: one favored keeping it based on existing production coverage, while others proposed moving it to draft, citing the film’s early stage and limited production information.

2026.summary: Editors disagreed over how to present the league’s financial figures after transactions shifted to Pakistani rupees: one favored a fixed U.S.-dollar comparison in a footnote, while another argued that currency-conversion templates better reflected amounts paid in rupees. They also disputed whether conversions based on changing exchange rates could mislead readers, with one editor calling the template’s figures inaccurate and the other saying that fixed dollar values would not match the exchange rate when payments were made.

2024.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the article’s impact section should remain: one view was that it was too soon to judge the album’s effect and that some material belonged in the article about its single, while another pointed to increased visibility and chart success for Black country artists as evidence of broader impact. A narrower approach was also proposed, retaining discussion of that visibility while limiting claims about the album’s overall effects.

2025.summary: Editors disputed which reported box-office figures should be included, with one proposal to use India Today’s ₹80 crore and The Hindu’s ₹96.97 crore estimates alongside higher figures from other outlets. Others argued that the lower estimates were inconsistent or derived from an unreliable tracker, while their proponents said the outlets had independently reported them and that the article should reflect a range.

2024.summary: Editors disputed how prominently to feature a Yale Integrity Project paper criticizing the Cass Review: some called it a substantial counter-report by eight scholars, while others described it as self-published and lightly covered, arguing it merited little weight.

2026.summary: One editor asked for plot and cast details attributed to leaks to be removed, arguing that publishing them before the film’s release was unethical and could spoil the film for readers. Other editors argued that details covered by reliable secondary reporting could be included, and that Wikipedia should not omit them just to prevent spoilers or wait for official sources.

2025.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the opening paragraph should describe the tour as a stadium tour, with supporters pointing to sources that used that label and the promoter’s classification. An opponent argued that the tour also included arenas and that calling it a stadium tour was misleading, while supporters distinguished that label from an “all-stadium” tour, meaning every concert takes place in a stadium.

2024.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to keep an “Accomplishments” section highlighting countries’ first medals in particular sports: one argued the information was well sourced and should remain, while another said sourcing alone did not justify its inclusion and that these milestones were too niche for a medal table.

2025.summary: Editors debated whether coverage of the pre-release backlash over Yasuke should have its own section or be integrated into broader discussion: some supported a dedicated section, while others favored embedding the material instead.

2026.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include a Find Out Now poll that added Restore Britain and Your Party to its party list in the main results table: one editor removed it because the pollster said it should not be directly compared with other polls, while another supported inclusion because both parties existed and the poll came from a recognised pollster. Supporters argued that different party prompts alone did not justify excluding the results, while opponents considered the survey irregular because it differed from Find Out Now’s usual polling and was commissioned by Restore Britain.

2024.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the voting table should color-code the AI Arena winner, with one position reserving colors for roles that affect nominations or voting and treating the winner as an ordinary voter. Another editor argued that the winner’s immunity from eviction was an important game mechanic that should be shown, pointing to similar treatment of immunity in earlier seasons.
An editor proposed adding a Koimoi review, while another objected that the critic was not notable and the outlet was considered unreliable.

2026.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the episode 5 summary should name Adam Bourke, with one arguing his death leads to later events and another calling him a nonessential background character whose identity need not be included. They also disputed describing celebrity cameos as “cronies”: one editor preferred calling them friends because the discussion did not establish that they were part of a criminal group, while another said they helped expose fellow celebrities to advance their careers.

Editors disputed whether the political-issues section used partisan language and combined separate subjects to imply a political conclusion; one editor sought a more neutral, clearly attributed presentation, while another defended the wording as factual and objected to describing it as criticism of the voter-list process. They also disagreed over whether the opening paragraph should describe that process as an erosion of democracy or instead use language about purifying the voter list.

2025.summary: Editors differed over whether the Enderlin tornado’s EF-5 rating might later be reversed; one expressed doubt, pointing to the damage research behind the rating and contrasting it with the radar-based assessment of the 2013 El Reno tornado.

2024.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the events of August 4 and 5 were separate movements or parts of one continuing movement, and whether the protest should be considered over after August 5 or left open to continue. They also disputed whether reports about misinformation by Indian media justified describing the issue broadly as Indian media disinformation, with an editor arguing that the sources concerned only a few accounts rather than media outlets as a whole.

2025.summary: Editors disagreed over whether Michelle Obama belonged on the list of potential candidates: one position was that recent media coverage met the article’s source-based criteria and she had not specifically ruled out a 2028 run, while others argued that speculation or her repeated expressions of disinterest did not justify including her. The discussion’s recorded outcome was that she should not be included, while the broader question of whether to remove the potential-candidate sections was left for a separate discussion.

2024.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the opening paragraph should mention claims of disinformation by Indian media: some argued this repeated a point covered elsewhere and risked sounding accusatory, while others said the issue belonged in the overview because it was documented by reliable sources. They also disagreed over whether to keep a section specifically about disinformation or rename it more broadly as “Media coverage.”

2025.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to keep a separate section about critics’ reactions to the song’s inclusion on the album or condense it into the general critical-reception section; one editor argued that much of the commentary concerned the song’s placement and gave that angle too much space. Another editor argued that reviewers had treated the song’s inclusion as a distinct point of criticism, sometimes their main comment about it, and that merging the material could lose that context.

Editors disagreed over whether the article should list the game’s Grand Game Awards recognition: one editor said awards should be included only when covered by reliable secondary sources, while another argued that the event had sufficient coverage and asked for its awards to be restored. The disagreement also involved whether the cited outlets met Wikipedia’s reliability standards.

Editors disagreed over whether “Die with a Smile” should be listed as a single from Mayhem, given that it was released before the album and was initially described as a standalone single. One editor argued it should be excluded from the album’s singles list because “Disease” began the album’s promotional release sequence, while another argued that its later inclusion on the album and in promotional materials supported listing it as an album single.

Editors debated how to format the entry for a contestant representing Miss Universe Latina, which is described as a non-country entrant: one editor favored a flag-like marker for consistent alignment, while another argued that no flag should appear because it could imply nationhood.

2026.summary: Editors disagreed over how much space the article should give criticism of the film’s historical accuracy: one proposed reducing extensive coverage to a short summary, while another argued that substantial coverage was justified by the attention the subject had received. They also differed on presentation, with some favoring a condensed account and others preferring brief paraphrases placed alongside the sections about casting, design, and other subjects rather than gathered in one place.

2025.summary: Editors disputed how to describe Norway’s participation: one comment noted that Norway was not among the countries announced as non-participants, while another said a cited source showed its broadcaster would not take part.
Editors disputed the reported box-office total for *They Call Him OG*: one requested changing it from 361 crore to 270 crore, while the reply said a revised figure of 283.5 crore was more accurate.

2026.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the article should say the film reached No. 1 on streaming-store charts: one side argued the claim was misleading without clearer timing and context, while another said the chart placement was worth retaining and could be worded more precisely. They also disputed describing reviews in the opening paragraph as “overwhelmingly negative,” with one editor objecting that this overstated a limited set of early reviews and another arguing that the available critical coverage supported the stronger description.

2025.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to call Musk’s action a “gesture” or a “salute”: some argued that “salute” was more precise and reflected how sources described it, while others said that wording treated a disputed interpretation as fact and preferred the more neutral “gesture.” They also disputed how the opening paragraph should describe the allegation, including whether to say it was interpreted by some as a Nazi or fascist salute or instead state that it resembled one; editors noted that a change in framing needed broader discussion.ф

Editors disagreed over whether the title should use the passenger flight’s number, following examples of other aviation articles, or describe a collision involving both aircraft; opponents said a flight-only title left out the helicopter and the collision itself. They also debated how to name the passenger flight in the opening paragraph: some favored PSA Airlines, which operated it, while others preferred American Eagle, the name they said the public encountered when booking and traveling.

Editors disagreed over whether to count a weak California tornado from March 13 as part of the outbreak: some connected it to the same storm system, while others argued that its location and timing set it apart from the later tornado activity. They also debated whether the title should cover only the main tornado days, extend to include a later North Carolina tornado, or use a broader name for the storm system and its other effects.

Editors disputed whether the opening paragraph should say the film’s premise had been rejected by scientists: some argued that available criticism did not establish a broad rejection, while others considered the cited scientists’ comments sufficient to support that wording. They also disputed whether a NASA panel member had reviewed classified evidence; one account linked the panel’s work to classified congressional testimony, while other participants pointed to statements that the panel examined unclassified or public-domain information.

Editors disagreed over whether the promotional concerts should be merged into the separate Mayhem Ball tour article or kept in their own article, with some favoring a merge and others proposing to keep the articles separate while adding selected concert figures here. They also disagreed over whether updated reporting that counted the Mexico City and Singapore shows as part of the tour justified changing how the concerts were presented, and whether the shared show concept meant the tour should be renamed.

Editors disagreed over whether to list Diogo Jota’s death in the season article’s transfers-out table: some argued that death is not a transfer and he remained contracted, while others said the table should record his departure from the squad and the reason.
