Editors disagreed over whether the article should describe the party’s ideology as combining left- and right-wing ideas: one argued that sources supported calling it syncretic, while others said the sources did not use that label and that applying it went beyond what they established.

2026.summary: Editors disputed whether the party should be labeled far-left in the infobox or whether its political position should reflect sources describing right-wing or nationalist elements alongside left-wing ones. One position was that much of this criticism concerned MAGA Communism or individual leaders rather than the party itself, and that the far-left label and historical context should remain; another argued that outside sources linking the party to those ideas should guide its description, rather than the party’s own identification.

2025.summary: Editors disputed whether to name the accused in the article, with supporters arguing that reliable sources widely reported his name and that he had become more publicly known. Opponents argued that he was a private person who had been a minor at the time and had not been convicted, so the name should remain out.

Editors disagreed over whether the article should include a list of cardinals discussed as possible future popes, with some arguing such coverage was relevant if limited and consistently sourced, and others questioning whether it belonged in an encyclopedia article at all. Those favoring inclusion proposed a short prose account of a few names, while critics said combining separate media lists could require editors to make subjective choices or draw conclusions that no source stated directly.

2026.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include a Mainstreet poll: one argued its coverage by reliable sources justified including it and that calling it a “push poll” was an editor’s opinion, while another said the poll did not support the claim attached to it and that a reliable source alone was not enough. They also disagreed over how to present nomination contestants, with some favoring an alphabetical bullet list for readability and another objecting that the article should use prose, as other by-election articles did.

2025.summary: Editors disputed how to describe the Muridke complex struck by India: one proposal emphasized reports that the Pakistani government had taken it over and that it contained civilian facilities, while another argued that reporting indicated the site remained linked to militant activity. They also questioned whether reports about the Muridke complex and the nearby Nangal Sahadan site had been conflated, with a proposal to discuss them separately.

Editors disagreed over whether the article should list countries that had not competed for many years: some questioned the relevance of recording non-participation when countries were not expected to enter, while others argued that withdrawals connected to the Israel controversy warranted coverage and should be distinguished from longstanding absences.

2026.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include details of internal selection processes in a provisional-countries section: one argued such details had previously been included and would later move to country pages, while another said they risked duplicating information already listed.

Editors disagreed over whether to add reports of negative user responses to the reception section, with one proposing material based on YouTube comments and a Reddit community post and another arguing those sources were unsuitable and the information lacked coverage in secondary sources. The objection was that such material relied on user-generated content and amounted to original analysis rather than reporting established as important by secondary sources.

2025.summary: Editors disputed whether to include a lawyer’s theory that a water-pipe leak reset the engine controls: one argued it conflicted with the preliminary report’s account of fuel-cutoff switches moving, while another said unsupported theories like this should be excluded.

2026.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the preliminary report’s recorded fuel-switch transitions could be presented as identifying a cause of the crash: one argued the report did not establish a cause, while another said other reporting supported interpreting its findings. They also disputed whether the article’s short summary should mention fuel cutoff and the engines’ loss of thrust, or simply state that the crash remained under investigation.

Editors disputed whether the article should describe Restore Britain as far-right or right-wing, and whether differences in sources justified presenting both labels rather than giving greater weight to far-right descriptions. A July request for comment closed with the decision that the opening paragraph and infobox should use only “far-right,” based on the view that most reliable sources use that label.

Editors disputed whether the article should state in its own voice that Advance UK is far-right or attribute that label to sources. Some argued that the label was supported by the weight of sources and earlier discussion, while others said sources used differing descriptions and that the article should reflect those differences.

2025.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include a short CNN discussion linking a prior climate study to the floods: supporters viewed it as useful background, while opponents argued it did not establish a connection to this event and gave the article too much weight. They also disputed how to describe Kerr County’s unused federal funds, including whether to mention local political conservatism and how many residents opposed the funds; one position favored that context, while another objected to the wording and to implying that officials should have spent the money on flood warnings.

Editors disagreed over whether Your Party already existed as a political party or was still being formed, and whether the article should describe the organisation or the process of its creation. They also disputed how much Labour history belonged in the article: one proposal sought a detailed account of developments from 2015 onward as context for the party’s formation, while critics argued that much of this history was not directly connected to the new party.

2026.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to include Gaenari’s monsoon-depression classification: one argued that its appearance in best-track data supported including it, while another said monsoon depressions are not tropical cyclones and should not be labeled as such.

Editors disputed whether the year article’s “maximum rated tornado” entry should include the Turkey–Syria tornado, rated IF3, alongside the Enid tornado, rated EF4; some argued that wind-speed estimates made the events comparable, while others said the entry should follow rating numbers rather than estimated winds. The discussion also raised whether to describe the Turkey–Syria tornado as the year’s strongest, but editors questioned comparing estimates across different rating scales, and no source in the discussion was identified as making that overall claim.

Editors disputed whether the article should describe the tour as promoting the album *Positions*, which had been included on the basis of a media report but was considered unnecessary by some editors. The discussion contrasted coverage describing the tour as spanning *Positions* and *Eternal Sunshine* with a tour promoter’s release, which named *Eternal Sunshine* and its deluxe edition as the supported albums.

2025.summary: Editors disputed whether the article title should describe Kirk’s death as an assassination or use the more general term killing: supporters argued that reliable sources increasingly used assassination for the targeted killing of a politically prominent figure, while opponents said coverage remained mixed and that the suspect’s guilt and motive were not established.

2026.summary: Editors disputed whether Mike Colter should appear in the season’s main cast listing: some favored placing him there based on the show’s usual crediting approach and his reported major role, while others said the available sources did not confirm his billing for this season. Those opposing the listing argued that presenting him as main cast would make an unverified future credit look like a confirmed fact; supporters said the placement was provisional until season-specific credits became available.

2025.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the article should include elimination charts for the series, with a proposal to add them met by objections that they lacked independent coverage and would take up too much space. They also disputed whether the opening paragraph should say that the series influenced the emergence of “object shows”: one editor considered that point important enough to include, while another argued that it was not prominent enough in the article to belong there.

2026.summary: Editors disagreed over whether to expand the reception section: one proposed finding more reviews, while others said available coverage was too limited or too weak to justify adding material. They also disputed whether the show should be described as made for children, with one editor saying the cited sources did not support that label and another arguing that existing coverage supported at least a children’s category; discussion also touched on describing its audience in the opening paragraph.

Editors disputed whether to retain details of several attacks and injuries: one argued that a later daily casualty total did not replace the specific event details, while another said the incidents would be duplicated in the timeline.

2025.summary: Editors disagreed over whether research linking climate change to Melissa’s intensity should have a separate section or be integrated into the storm’s meteorological history; some argued it warranted distinct treatment, while others said a dedicated section gave the topic disproportionate emphasis. They also questioned whether estimates such as a fourfold increase in likelihood were defined precisely enough to describe this particular storm.

2026.summary: Editors disagreed over whether the opening paragraph should describe Storrie as an Emmy-nominated actor: one argued the nomination should be included among his accomplishments, while another said the paragraph should identify him without promotional award language.

Editors disagreed over whether to call the attack an “Islamic terrorist attack”: one view pointed to the attackers’ reported religious practice and ISIS inspiration, while opponents said ISIS-inspired terrorism was supported but the broader label implied a religious motive the sources did not establish. They also debated whether to include the accused men’s nationality and residency in the opening paragraph, with supporters arguing that it mattered that they were not foreign actors and an alternative proposal leaving those details out.

Editors disagreed over whether the article should call the film propaganda outright: some argued that critics widely used the label, while others said it should be presented only as an attributed criticism rather than as fact. They also debated the opening wording, with proposals ranging from calling it a propaganda film to describing it as a documentary or a film using a documentary format before discussing the criticism.

Editors disagreed over whether the opening paragraph should focus on Nick Shirley’s video and the political response to it, or give more attention to the wider range of Minnesota fraud cases. Some favored the video-focused version as a better reflection of the story’s prominence, while others argued that a broader account better represented the article as a whole.

Editors disagreed over whether to include a Piper PA-28 crash: one argued that the deaths of the pilot and flight instructor and the aircraft’s impact with a house made it noteworthy, while others rejected the listing as not noteworthy.

Editors disagreed over whether a guilty plea by the owner of a daycare featured in Shirley’s video meant the video’s fraud allegations should no longer be described as unsubstantiated. Some argued the plea supported Shirley’s claims, while others said the charged conduct did not include the alleged inflation of attendance figures and that sources had not connected the plea to his specific claims.

Editors disagreed over whether the article should mention reports suggesting Good was observing immigration enforcement activity, with one editor proposing an account of the claims and another saying the cited coverage did not establish that she belonged to an organized group. The responding editor also noted that the article already included state officials’ view that Good was acting as a legal observer.

Editors disagreed over whether the title should say “shooting” or “shootings”: some argued that the attacks at two locations warranted the plural, while others described them as one connected event and favored the singular. They also disputed whether female pronouns should continue after the perpetrator’s death; one editor argued the guidance did not apply after death, while others said it applied to articles mentioning people.

Editors debated whether the article’s title should describe a broader Iran conflict or focus on the initial Israeli and U.S. strikes; proponents of a broader title pointed to Iran’s retaliation, while others said it was too soon to call the events a war. The move discussion settled on “2026 Iran conflict” for the time being, with no agreement to use “2026 Iran war.”

Editors disputed whether the article should describe the album as co-written by Grande and Ilya: one editor said Grande wrote the lyrics alone but that the songs were not written by her alone. The other argued that “writer” could imply Ilya wrote lyrics and preferred wording that identified Grande as lyricist and Ilya as composer.

Editors disagreed over whether to show co-producers in a dedicated column alongside the tracks or list their credits only in the personnel section. One editor argued that a column would mostly repeat the main producer’s name because only three tracks had co-producers, while others said track-by-track credits would make those contributions easier for readers to find. The discussion also noted that there was no universal guideline for this formatting choice and that it was handled case by case.

Editors disagreed over whether the article should present Abhijeet Dipke as the movement’s founder and central figure or give more weight to the claim that the movement grew from wider youth participation and that Dipke mainly gathered existing support. A separate proposal sought an article about Dipke, while a later edit request asked to add wider youth context to the article’s opening paragraph.

Editors disputed whether to describe the murder weapon as a kirpan, a Sikh religious knife, or by a more specific type such as a pesh-kabz dagger. Some argued that the prosecution and judge treated it as a kirpan, while others favored the more specific label and cited Sikh authorities who distinguished it from a kirpan.
